summary.en: Roman legions under Titus besieged Jerusalem during the First Jewish–Roman War. The city fell in late summer 70 and the Second Temple was destroyed, a turning point for Judaism and for Jewish life in Judaea.
summary.zh: 第一次犹太-罗马战争期间，提图斯率罗马军团围攻耶路撒冷。公元70年夏末城破，第二圣殿被毁，成为犹太教历史和犹地亚犹太人生活的转折点。

sources.title: Josephus, The Jewish War, Books V–VI

story.en:
In 66 CE a revolt against Roman rule spread through Judaea, and by 70 Vespasian's son Titus had ringed Jerusalem with four legions. Inside, rival Jewish factions under John of Gischala and Simon bar Giora had fought each other and burned grain stores, so famine set in early. The Romans built ramps, broke through the city's three walls one after another and stormed the Antonia fortress beside the Temple.

Josephus, a Jewish commander who had gone over to the Romans and watched from their camp, claims Titus wished to spare the Temple, but it burned in the late summer of 70; Jewish tradition later fixed its loss on the fast of Tisha B'Av. The upper city fell weeks afterwards.

Titus paraded the Temple treasures, including the menorah, through Rome, a scene still carved on his arch. Without the Temple and its sacrifices, Judaism reorganised around rabbis, study and the synagogue.
story.zh:
66年，犹地亚爆发反抗罗马统治的起义；到70年，韦斯巴芗之子提图斯率四个军团包围了耶路撒冷。城内由吉斯卡拉的约翰和西门·巴尔·吉奥拉分别率领的犹太派系相互厮杀，还焚毁了粮仓，饥荒很早就降临。罗马人修筑攻城坡道，逐一突破三道城墙，攻占了圣殿旁的安东尼亚堡。

投降罗马、在罗马营中亲眼目睹战事的犹太将领约瑟夫斯声称，提图斯本想保全圣殿，但圣殿仍在70年夏末被焚毁；犹太传统后来把这一日子定在埃波月初九（圣殿被毁日）的斋戒。数周之后上城也告失守。

提图斯把包括七枝灯台在内的圣殿宝物带回罗马游行示众，这一场景至今仍刻在他的凯旋门上。失去圣殿与献祭之后，犹太教转而以拉比、经典研习和会堂为中心重新组织起来。

summary.en: Simon bar Kokhba led a Jewish uprising in Judaea against Hadrian, provoked in part by plans to refound Jerusalem as the Roman colony Aelia Capitolina. Its suppression, ending at Betar, devastated Judaea, and the province was renamed Syria Palaestina.
summary.zh: 西蒙·巴尔·科赫巴领导犹地亚犹太人反抗哈德良，起因之一是罗马计划把耶路撒冷重建为殖民城市爱利亚加比多连。起义最终在贝塔尔被镇压，犹地亚遭到重创，行省更名为叙利亚-巴勒斯坦。

note: Plotted at Betar (modern Battir), the revolt's last stronghold, taken in 135/136.

name.en: Battle of Hormozdgan (founding of the Sasanian Empire)
name.zh: 霍尔木兹甘之战（萨珊王朝建立）

summary.en: Ardashir, a Persian vassal king from Fars, defeated and killed the Parthian king Artabanus IV. The victory ended nearly five centuries of Arsacid rule and founded the Sasanian Empire, which rivalled Rome for four hundred years.
summary.zh: 法尔斯的波斯藩王阿尔达希尔击败并杀死安息国王阿尔达班四世。此战结束了阿萨息斯王朝近五百年的统治，建立了此后与罗马抗衡四百年的萨珊王朝。

sources.title: al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings, vol. V (trans. Bosworth)

note: The battlefield has not been located; the date 28 April 224 is the conventional reconstruction.

story.en:
Ardashir began as a local ruler in Fars, the old Persian heartland around Istakhr. In the early 220s he subdued neighbouring princes without leave from his Parthian overlord, Artabanus IV, and the king finally marched against him. The two armies met on the plain of Hormozdgan, whose location is still unknown; the conventional date is 28 April 224.

Artabanus was killed. A rock relief at Firuzabad shows the battle as a series of mounted duels, with Ardashir unhorsing the Parthian king and his son Shapur overthrowing another noble, an image of personal combat that the new dynasty used to proclaim its right to rule.

Ardashir took the title "King of Kings of Iran" and within a few years held Ctesiphon. The Sasanian dynasty he founded ruled for more than four centuries, centralised government more than the Arsacids had, promoted Zoroastrianism and fought Rome as an equal.
story.zh:
阿尔达希尔起初只是法尔斯（以伊斯塔赫尔为中心的古波斯腹地）的一位地方统治者。220年代初，他未经宗主安息国王阿尔达班四世许可便征服了邻近诸侯，国王终于亲征讨伐。两军在霍尔木兹甘平原交战，其确切地点至今不明，传统上定在224年4月28日。

阿尔达班阵亡。菲鲁扎巴德的一处摩崖浮雕把这场战役刻画为一连串骑马单挑：阿尔达希尔把安息国王挑落马下，其子沙普尔也击倒了另一名贵族。新王朝借这种亲身搏杀的形象来宣示统治的正当性。

阿尔达希尔自称“伊朗的万王之王”，数年内占领泰西封。他开创的萨珊王朝统治了四百多年，比阿萨息斯王朝更为中央集权，扶持琐罗亚斯德教，并以对等之势与罗马抗衡。

summary.en: Shapur I defeated a Roman army near Edessa and captured Emperor Valerian, the first Roman emperor taken prisoner by a foreign enemy. Shapur commemorated the triumph in rock reliefs and in his trilingual inscription at Naqsh-e Rostam.
summary.zh: 沙普尔一世在埃德萨附近击败罗马军队，俘虏皇帝瓦勒良——这是第一位被外敌俘获的罗马皇帝。沙普尔在纳克什-鲁斯塔姆以浮雕和三语铭文纪念此役。

sources.title: Shapur I, inscription on the Ka'ba-ye Zartosht (ŠKZ), Naqsh-e Rostam

note: Usually dated 260; some scholars prefer 259.

story.en:
Shapur I had already defeated the army of Gordian III and made Philip the Arab pay for peace when, around 260, his armies besieged Edessa and Carrhae in upper Mesopotamia. Emperor Valerian marched to relieve them with an army weakened, by some accounts, by plague. Near Edessa the Romans were defeated, and Valerian was taken while trying to negotiate; Roman writers disagree on whether he was seized by treachery or captured in battle.

Shapur boasted of the victory in his trilingual inscription at Naqsh-e Rostam, the "Res Gestae Divi Saporis", which lists the Roman provinces from which his soldiers came. Rock reliefs show Valerian standing captive beside the mounted king. Later Christian authors told lurid stories that Shapur used him as a footstool and had him flayed, but these are hostile legends.

Valerian died in captivity. Roman deportees were settled in Persian cities such as Bishapur and Gundeshapur, where they helped build bridges and dams, including the dam-bridge at Shushtar.
story.zh:
沙普尔一世此前已击败戈尔迪安三世的军队，并迫使“阿拉伯人”菲利普出钱求和。约260年，他的军队围攻上美索不达米亚的埃德萨与卡莱。罗马皇帝瓦勒良率军驰援，据一些记载，这支军队已被瘟疫削弱。罗马军在埃德萨附近战败，瓦勒良在谈判时被俘；罗马作家对他究竟是中计被擒还是战场被俘说法不一。

沙普尔在纳克什·鲁斯塔姆的三语铭文（即《沙普尔功业录》）中夸耀这场胜利，并列出其士兵所来自的罗马行省。摩崖浮雕中，瓦勒良作为俘虏站在骑马的国王身旁。后来的基督教作者编造了沙普尔以他当垫脚凳、将他剥皮等骇人故事，但这些都是敌意传说。

瓦勒良死于囚禁之中。被俘的罗马人被安置在比沙普尔、贡迪沙普尔等波斯城市，参与修建桥梁和水坝，其中包括舒什塔尔的坝桥。

summary.en: According to Armenian tradition, King Tiridates III was converted by Gregory the Illuminator and made Christianity the religion of his kingdom, the first state to adopt it officially. The cathedral of Etchmiadzin was founded at the royal city of Vagharshapat.
summary.zh: 据亚美尼亚传统，国王梯里达底三世受启蒙者格列高利感化而皈依，并定基督教为国教，使亚美尼亚成为第一个正式奉基督教为国教的国家。埃奇米阿津大教堂建于王城瓦加尔沙帕特。

note: Traditional date 301; many historians prefer c. 314.

story.en:
Armenian tradition, set down in the 5th-century history attributed to Agathangelos, tells the story this way. King Tiridates III had Gregory, a Christian of Parthian noble descent, thrown into a pit at Khor Virap for refusing to sacrifice to the goddess Anahit, and he lay there for some thirteen years. When the king fell into madness after martyring a group of Christian nuns, Gregory was brought out, healed him and baptised the royal court.

Tiridates then made Christianity the religion of his kingdom, which is why Armenia is often called the first Christian state. Gregory was consecrated bishop at Caesarea in Cappadocia, and the cathedral of Etchmiadzin rose at Vagharshapat. The traditional date is 301; many modern historians prefer about 314, close to Gregory's consecration.

Royal adoption set Armenia apart from both Rome, where Christianity was at best newly tolerated, and Zoroastrian Persia, and the Church became the backbone of Armenian identity through centuries of foreign rule.
story.zh:
据署名阿加坦格罗斯的5世纪亚美尼亚史书记载：国王梯里达底三世因格里高利（一位有安息贵族血统的基督徒）拒绝向女神阿娜希特献祭，把他投进霍尔维拉普的深坑，他在坑中被关了约十三年。国王在杀害一群基督教修女后陷入癫狂，人们把格里高利从坑中救出，他治好了国王，并为王室成员施洗。

此后梯里达底把基督教定为王国的宗教，因此亚美尼亚常被称为第一个基督教国家。格里高利在卡帕多西亚的凯撒里亚被祝圣为主教，埃奇米阿津大教堂在瓦加尔沙帕特落成。传统年份为301年，不少现代史家倾向于格里高利受祝圣前后的约314年。

王室皈依使亚美尼亚既有别于基督教至多刚获宽容的罗马，也有别于信奉琐罗亚斯德教的波斯；在此后数百年的异族统治下，教会成为亚美尼亚民族认同的支柱。

summary.en: Emperor Constantine convened bishops from across the empire at Nicaea in Bithynia. The council rejected Arianism, issued the original Nicene Creed and set common rules such as the method of dating Easter. It is counted as the first ecumenical council.
summary.zh: 君士坦丁皇帝召集帝国各地主教在比提尼亚的尼西亚开会。会议否定阿里乌派，颁布最初的《尼西亚信经》，并统一了复活节日期的推算等规定，被视为第一次大公会议。

sources.title: Eusebius, Life of Constantine, Book III

story.en:
The dispute began in Alexandria, where the priest Arius taught that the Son of God was created by the Father and so not eternal. Bishop Alexander condemned him, and the quarrel split churches across the East. Constantine, newly master of the whole empire and eager for a united Church, summoned bishops to Nicaea in Bithynia in 325, paying for their travel through the imperial post.

Around 250–300 bishops attended (later tradition fixed the number at 318), many from the Greek East. The emperor himself opened the sessions. The council adopted a creed declaring the Son "of one substance" (homoousios) with the Father, condemned Arius, and issued canons on church discipline and a common way of calculating Easter.

Nicaea did not end the Arian controversy, which raged for another half century, but it set the precedent of empire-wide councils called by the emperor. A revised form of its creed is still recited by most Christian churches.
story.zh:
争论起于亚历山大城：神父阿里乌教导说，圣子为圣父所造，因而并非永恒。亚历山大主教谴责了他，争执随即使东方各地教会分裂。刚刚统一全帝国、渴望教会团结的君士坦丁，于325年召集各地主教前往比提尼亚的尼西亚，并让他们使用帝国驿站往返。

与会主教约有二百五十至三百人（后世传统定为318人），多数来自希腊语东方。皇帝亲自主持开幕。会议通过信经，宣告圣子与圣父“同质”（homoousios），谴责阿里乌，并颁布有关教会纪律的教规以及统一推算复活节的方法。

尼西亚会议并未结束阿里乌派之争，此后争论又持续了半个世纪；但它开创了由皇帝召集全帝国大公会议的先例。其信经的修订本至今仍为大多数基督教会诵念。

summary.en: The monk Mesrop Mashtots, supported by King Vramshapuh and Catholicos Sahak, devised a 36-letter alphabet for Armenian. It launched the translation of the Bible and a native literature that anchored Armenian identity.
summary.zh: 修士梅斯罗普·马什托茨在国王弗拉姆沙普和大主教萨哈克支持下，为亚美尼亚语创制了36个字母。由此开始了《圣经》翻译和本土文学创作，奠定了亚美尼亚民族认同。

note: c. 405 following Koriun; exact year debated.

summary.en: The fourth ecumenical council, meeting at Chalcedon across the Bosporus from Constantinople, defined Christ as one person in two natures. Many Christians in Egypt, Syria and Armenia rejected it, producing the lasting split between Chalcedonian and Oriental Orthodox churches.
summary.zh: 第四次大公会议在君士坦丁堡对岸的迦克墩召开，确定基督为“一个位格、两种本性”。埃及、叙利亚和亚美尼亚的许多基督徒拒绝这一定义，形成迦克墩派与东方正统教会之间的长期分裂。

sources.title: R. Price & M. Gaddis (trans.), The Acts of the Council of Chalcedon (2005)

summary.en: A powerful earthquake, followed by fire, destroyed much of Antioch, one of the great cities of the Eastern Roman Empire. Chroniclers reported about 250,000 deaths, probably an exaggeration but a sign of immense devastation.
summary.zh: 一场强烈地震及随后的大火摧毁了东罗马帝国大城安条克的大部分地区。编年史家记载死者约25万人，虽可能夸大，但足见灾难之惨烈。

sources.title: E. Guidoboni, Catalogue of Ancient Earthquakes in the Mediterranean Area up to the 10th Century (1994)

summary.en: The last and most destructive war between Rome and Persia. Khosrow II's armies took Syria, Jerusalem and Egypt, but Heraclius counter-attacked through the Caucasus, won near Nineveh in 627 and forced peace, leaving both empires exhausted on the eve of the Arab conquests.
summary.zh: 罗马与波斯之间最后也是最具破坏性的战争。霍斯劳二世的军队夺取叙利亚、耶路撒冷和埃及，但希拉克略经高加索反攻，627年在尼尼微附近获胜并迫使波斯议和，两大帝国在阿拉伯征服前夕均已精疲力竭。

sources.title: J. Howard-Johnston, The Last Great War of Antiquity (2021)

note: Plotted near Nineveh, site of the decisive battle of 627.

story.en:
When the emperor Maurice was murdered by the usurper Phocas in 602, Khosrow II of Persia, whom Maurice had once helped back to his throne, declared war to avenge him. The Persians exploited Roman civil strife brilliantly: they took Antioch in 613, Jerusalem in 614, carrying off the relic believed to be the True Cross, and Egypt by 619. In 626 a Persian army stood on the Bosporus while Avars besieged Constantinople.

Heraclius, emperor since 610, gambled on striking at Persia's heart. Allied with the Western Turks, he campaigned through Armenia and the Caucasus, and in December 627 he defeated the Persian army near the ruins of Nineveh. Khosrow was overthrown and killed by his own son early in 628, and peace restored the old frontier.

Heraclius returned the Cross to Jerusalem in 630, but both empires were drained of men and money. Within a decade Arab armies took Syria from one and Iraq from the other.
story.zh:
602年，皇帝莫里斯被篡位者福卡斯杀害。曾得莫里斯之助复位的波斯国王库思老二世以复仇为名宣战。波斯人巧妙利用罗马内乱：613年攻占安条克，614年攻占耶路撒冷并夺走被信为“真十字架”的圣物，619年前后又夺取埃及。626年，波斯大军驻扎在博斯普鲁斯海峡对岸，阿瓦尔人则围攻君士坦丁堡。

自610年在位的希拉克略决定孤注一掷，直捣波斯腹地。他与西突厥结盟，转战亚美尼亚与高加索，627年12月在尼尼微废墟附近击败波斯军。628年初，库思老被亲生儿子推翻并处死，和约恢复了旧有边界。

630年，希拉克略将十字架送回耶路撒冷，但两大帝国都已人财两空。不到十年，阿拉伯军队便从前者手中夺取叙利亚，从后者手中夺取伊拉克。

summary.en: Islamic tradition holds that Muhammad, meditating in the cave of Hira on a mountain above Mecca, received the first verses of the Qur'an through the angel Gabriel. Muslims regard this as the beginning of his prophethood.
summary.zh: 据伊斯兰传统，穆罕默德在麦加附近山上的希拉山洞中静修时，经天使吉卜利勒（加百列）接受了《古兰经》最初的经文。穆斯林视此为其使命的开端。

sources.title: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (trans. A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad, 1955)

note: Traditional date c. 610.

story.en:
According to Islamic tradition, Muhammad, then about forty and a respected merchant of Mecca, used to retreat to a small cave called Hira on Jabal al-Nur, a mountain north-east of the city, to meditate. One night in the month of Ramadan, the accounts say, the angel Gabriel appeared and commanded him "Recite!" (iqra). After protesting that he could not, he received the opening verses of what Muslims hold to be Sura 96 of the Qur'an.

The early biographies describe him returning home shaken and asking his wife Khadija to cover him. She comforted him and took him to her Christian cousin Waraqa ibn Nawfal, who reportedly told him he had been visited as Moses had. Khadija is remembered as the first person to accept his message.

Revelations continued for some twenty-two years until Muhammad's death in 632. Muslims commemorate the first one on Laylat al-Qadr, the "Night of Power", late in Ramadan.
story.zh:
据伊斯兰传统记载，时年约四十岁、在麦加颇受敬重的商人穆罕默德，常到城东北光明山上一个名为希拉的小山洞中静修。传述说，在莱麦丹月的一个夜晚，天使吉卜利勒（加百列）显现，命令他“你读！”。他推辞说自己不会读，随后领受了穆斯林所认为的《古兰经》第96章开头几节。

早期传记说他惊魂未定地回到家中，请妻子赫蒂彻为他盖上衣被。赫蒂彻安慰他，并带他去见她信奉基督教的堂兄瓦拉盖·本·瑙法勒；据说瓦拉盖告诉他，他所遇到的正是曾降临穆萨（摩西）的那位使者。赫蒂彻被尊为第一个接受其信仰的人。

此后启示持续了约二十二年，直到穆罕默德632年去世。穆斯林在莱麦丹月下旬的“盖德尔夜”纪念首次启示。

summary.en: Facing hostility in Mecca, Muhammad and his followers migrated to Yathrib, thereafter called Medina, where he founded the first Muslim community. The year of the migration later became the epoch of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar.
summary.zh: 因在麦加受到敌视，穆罕默德与追随者迁往叶斯里卜（此后称麦地那），建立了第一个穆斯林社团。迁徙之年后来成为伊斯兰教历（希吉拉历）的纪元。

sources.title: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (trans. Guillaume)

story.en:
In Mecca, Muhammad's preaching against idol worship threatened the leading Quraysh families, who profited from pilgrims to the Kaaba. After the deaths of his wife Khadija and his protective uncle Abu Talib around 619, the pressure grew. Pilgrims from Yathrib, an oasis some 340 km to the north torn by feuds between its Arab tribes, invited him to come as an arbiter and pledged to protect him.

His followers slipped away in small groups. According to the traditional accounts, Muhammad left last with Abu Bakr, hid for three days in the cave of Thawr south of Mecca while Quraysh searchers passed by, and then took a roundabout route, reaching Quba outside Yathrib in September 622.

The oasis became Medina, "the City" of the Prophet, where he built a mosque and drew up an agreement among its communities. Some seventeen years later the caliph Umar chose the year of the migration as the starting point of the Islamic calendar.
story.zh:
在麦加，穆罕默德反对偶像崇拜的宣教威胁到了靠克尔白朝圣者获利的古莱什望族。约619年，妻子赫蒂彻和庇护他的伯父艾布·塔利卜相继去世，压力日增。来自叶斯里卜的朝圣者邀请他前去调解当地阿拉伯部落之间的世仇，并誓言保护他；那是一片位于麦加以北约340公里、为内斗所困的绿洲。

他的追随者分成小队悄然离开。据传统记载，穆罕默德与艾布·伯克尔最后出发，在麦加以南的绍尔山洞中躲了三天，古莱什搜寻者从洞口经过而未发现，随后二人绕道而行，于622年9月抵达叶斯里卜郊外的库巴。

这片绿洲从此称为麦地那，即先知之“城”。他在此建清真寺，并与城中各群体订立盟约。约十七年后，哈里发欧麦尔把迁徙之年定为伊斯兰历的纪元。

summary.en: At the wells of Badr, a small Muslim force from Medina defeated a larger army of the Quraysh of Mecca. The victory, in the second year after the Hijra, greatly strengthened Muhammad's position in Arabia.
summary.zh: 在白德尔水井旁，麦地那的一支小规模穆斯林队伍击败了人数更多的麦加古莱什军队。这场发生在希吉拉后第二年的胜利大大巩固了穆罕默德在阿拉伯半岛的地位。

summary.en: Muhammad entered Mecca with a large army almost without bloodshed. The idols around the Kaaba were removed and most of the Quraysh accepted Islam, making Mecca the religious centre of the new faith.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德率大军几乎兵不血刃地进入麦加。克尔白周围的偶像被清除，古莱什人大多皈依伊斯兰教，麦加从此成为这一新宗教的中心。

sources.title: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (trans. Guillaume)

note: Wikidata gives 629; Muslim sources date it to Ramadan 8 AH, i.e. January 630 CE, which is used here.

story.en:
In 628 Muhammad and the Quraysh of Mecca agreed a ten-year truce at al-Hudaybiyya. When allies of the Quraysh attacked a tribe allied to the Muslims in late 629, Muhammad treated the truce as broken and marched on his home city with an army of about ten thousand, the traditional figure.

The Meccan leader Abu Sufyan came out to negotiate and accepted Islam. According to the accounts, Muhammad promised safety to anyone who stayed indoors, entered the Kaaba sanctuary or took refuge in Abu Sufyan's house, so the city was taken in January 630 with only a few clashes. Muhammad then circled the Kaaba and had the idols around it smashed; tradition says he recited the Qur'anic verse "Truth has come and falsehood has vanished".

He pardoned most of his former enemies. Mecca became the spiritual centre of Islam, and by Muhammad's death two years later most of the Arabian Peninsula had come under the authority of Medina.
story.zh:
628年，穆罕默德与麦加古莱什人在侯代比亚订立十年休战协议。629年末，古莱什的盟友袭击了与穆斯林结盟的部落，穆罕默德视休战已被破坏，率领传统记载中约一万人的军队向故乡进发。

麦加首领艾布·苏富扬出城谈判并皈依伊斯兰教。据记载，穆罕默德承诺：凡闭门不出者、进入克尔白禁地者或到艾布·苏富扬家中避难者，一律免于伤害。因此630年1月攻城时只发生了零星冲突。随后穆罕默德环绕克尔白巡行，下令砸毁周围的偶像；据传他诵读了“真理已来临，虚妄已消灭”这节经文。

他赦免了大多数昔日的敌人。麦加成为伊斯兰教的精神中心；两年后穆罕默德去世时，阿拉伯半岛大部分地区已归属麦地那的权威。

summary.en: Within a century of Muhammad's death, Arab Muslim armies under the Rashidun and Umayyad caliphs conquered the Sasanian Empire, Byzantine Syria and Egypt, North Africa, Iberia and parts of Central Asia, creating one of the largest empires in history and reshaping the region's religions and languages.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德去世后不到一个世纪，四大哈里发和倭马亚王朝的阿拉伯穆斯林军队征服了萨珊帝国、拜占庭的叙利亚和埃及、北非、伊比利亚及中亚部分地区，建立起历史上最大的帝国之一，深刻改变了该地区的宗教与语言。

label.zh: 梅尔夫；伊嗣俟三世之死

sources.title: H. Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)

note: Wikidata dates the overall process 622–750; here the start is 632, when expansion beyond Arabia began. Point is Wikidata's generic coordinate.

story.en:
After Muhammad died in 632, his successor Abu Bakr first reasserted Medina's authority over the Arabian tribes in the Ridda wars. From 633 Arab armies pushed into Iraq and Syria, both provinces of empires exhausted by their great war of 602–628. Decisive victories at Yarmouk (636) and al-Qadisiyyah (636 or 637) were followed by the capture of Jerusalem, Ctesiphon and, in 642, Alexandria.

Under the Umayyads the momentum continued: Carthage fell in 698, Iberia was invaded in 711, and Arab forces reached Transoxiana and Sindh. Expansion stalled only in the 730s and 740s, after defeats before Constantinople, in Gaul and against the Khazars and Turks.

The conquerors were few and at first ruled through existing officials and tax systems, settling in garrison towns such as Kufa, Basra and Fustat. Conversion to Islam and the spread of Arabic took centuries, but the conquests created a single political and commercial space from the Atlantic to the Indus.
story.zh:
632年穆罕默德去世后，继任者艾布·伯克尔先通过“叛教战争”重新确立了麦地那对阿拉伯各部落的权威。自633年起，阿拉伯军队进入伊拉克与叙利亚，这两地分属在602—628年大战中元气大伤的两大帝国。雅穆克（636年）与卡迪西亚（636或637年）两场决定性胜利之后，耶路撒冷、泰西封以及642年的亚历山大相继被攻克。

倭马亚王朝时期扩张势头不减：698年迦太基陷落，711年进军伊比利亚，阿拉伯军队远达河中地区和信德。直到730—740年代，在君士坦丁堡城下、高卢以及与可萨人、突厥人的作战中接连受挫，扩张才告停顿。

征服者人数不多，起初沿用原有的官吏和税制，聚居在库法、巴士拉、福斯塔特等军镇。皈依伊斯兰教和阿拉伯语的传播历经数百年，但这些征服造就了一个从大西洋延伸到印度河的统一政治与贸易空间。

summary.en: Over six days by the Yarmouk River, a Rashidun army commanded by Khalid ibn al-Walid destroyed a large Byzantine force. The defeat ended Byzantine rule in Syria and opened the Levant to Muslim rule.
summary.zh: 在雅尔穆克河畔历时六天的战斗中，哈立德·本·瓦利德指挥的正统哈里发军队歼灭了一支庞大的拜占庭军队。此役终结了拜占庭对叙利亚的统治，黎凡特由此归于穆斯林。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of the Yarmuk River
H. Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)

story.en:
After the Arab capture of Damascus, the emperor Heraclius gathered a large army of Byzantine regulars, Armenians and Christian Arab allies to retake Syria. The Muslim commanders, among them Khalid ibn al-Walid and Abu Ubayda, abandoned their recent gains and concentrated their forces on the plateau above the Yarmouk River, a tributary of the Jordan. Ancient figures for both armies are inflated; modern estimates vary widely.

The fighting lasted six days in August 636. The Byzantine side was hampered by divided command and quarrels among its contingents. On the final day Khalid's cavalry drove a wedge between the Byzantine horse and foot, and the trapped infantry was pushed back toward the ravines of the Wadi al-Raqqad, where many died.

Heraclius withdrew from Syria; tradition records his farewell to the province from Antioch. Jerusalem surrendered soon after, and Syria became the base from which the Umayyads would later rule the caliphate.
story.zh:
阿拉伯人攻占大马士革后，皇帝希拉克略集结了由拜占庭正规军、亚美尼亚人和信奉基督教的阿拉伯盟军组成的大军，意图收复叙利亚。哈立德·本·瓦利德、艾布·欧拜达等穆斯林将领放弃新近夺得的城镇，把兵力集中到约旦河支流雅穆克河上方的高原上。古代史料对双方兵力的记载都有夸大，现代估计出入很大。

战斗在636年8月持续了六天。拜占庭一方指挥不统一，各部之间矛盾重重。最后一天，哈立德的骑兵在拜占庭骑兵与步兵之间楔入，被截断的步兵被逼退到拉卡德谷地的峡谷边，大量丧生。

希拉克略撤出叙利亚；传统记载他在安条克向这片行省告别。不久耶路撒冷投降，叙利亚日后成为倭马亚王朝统治哈里发国的根据地。

summary.en: An Arab army under Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas defeated the Sasanian general Rostam Farrokhzad in several days of fighting near al-Hira. The victory opened Mesopotamia and the Sasanian capital Ctesiphon to the Muslims.
summary.zh: 赛义德·本·阿比·瓦卡斯率领的阿拉伯军队在希拉附近经数日激战击败萨珊将领鲁斯塔姆。此役为穆斯林打开了美索不达米亚和萨珊首都泰西封的大门。

sources.title: al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings, vol. XII (trans. Friedmann)

note: Wikidata and most modern works give November 636; some sources date it to 637.

story.en:
By 636 the young Sasanian king Yazdegerd III had entrusted his main army to Rostam Farrokhzad, who led it toward the Euphrates to stop the Arab advance into Iraq. The caliph Umar sent Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas against him with reinforcements, including veterans returning from Syria. The armies met at al-Qadisiyyah, south-west of al-Hira near the desert edge.

The battle lasted several days. The Persians fielded war elephants, which at first scattered the Arab horses until Arab warriors blinded and cut down the lead animals. The Muslim sources describe a final night of fighting followed by a wind that blew dust into Persian faces, and the death of Rostam himself; the details are told in heroic style and hard to verify.

The defeat broke Sasanian power west of the Zagros. The Arabs took the capital Ctesiphon in 637, and after Nahavand in 642 the empire collapsed; Yazdegerd fled east and was killed near Merv in 651.
story.zh:
到636年，年轻的萨珊国王伊嗣俟三世已把主力交给鲁斯塔姆·法罗赫扎德，命他率军前往幼发拉底河一线，阻止阿拉伯人深入伊拉克。哈里发欧麦尔派赛义德·本·艾比·瓦卡斯迎战，并调来包括从叙利亚回援老兵在内的援军。两军在希拉西南、沙漠边缘的卡迪西亚相遇。

战斗持续数日。波斯人投入战象，起初冲散了阿拉伯马队，直到阿拉伯勇士刺瞎并砍倒了领头的大象。穆斯林史料描述了最后一夜的鏖战，随后一阵大风把沙尘吹向波斯军，鲁斯塔姆本人也战死；这些细节带有英雄叙事色彩，难以一一核实。

此战摧毁了萨珊王朝在扎格罗斯山以西的力量。阿拉伯人于637年攻占都城泰西封，642年纳哈万德之战后帝国瓦解；伊嗣俟向东逃亡，651年在木鹿附近被杀。

summary.en: Arab forces defeated the last major Sasanian field army near Nahavand in the Zagros. Muslim chroniclers called it the "victory of victories"; afterwards Persian resistance fragmented and Yazdegerd III fled east.
summary.zh: 阿拉伯军队在扎格罗斯山区的纳哈万德附近击败萨珊最后一支主力野战军。穆斯林史家称之为“胜利中的胜利”；此后波斯抵抗分崩离析，伊嗣俟三世东逃。

sources.title: al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings, vol. XIII

note: Dated 642 (some sources 641). Wikidata's coordinates duplicate al-Qadisiyyah; plotted here at Nahavand town.

summary.en: Husayn ibn Ali, grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, was killed at Karbala with members of his family and companions by an army sent by the Umayyad governor of Kufa. His martyrdom on 10 Muharram (Ashura) is central to Shia Islam and commemorated every year.
summary.zh: 先知穆罕默德的外孙侯赛因·本·阿里及其家人、追随者在卡尔巴拉被倭马亚王朝库法总督派出的军队杀害。他于穆哈兰月十日（阿舒拉日）的殉难是什叶派信仰的核心，每年都被隆重纪念。

sources.title: al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings, vol. XIX (trans. Howard)

story.en:
When the caliph Mu'awiya died in 680, his son Yazid succeeded him, the first hereditary succession in Islam. Husayn, son of Ali and grandson of Muhammad, refused to pledge allegiance and accepted an invitation from supporters in Kufa to lead them. Before he arrived, the Umayyad governor Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad had crushed the movement in Kufa.

Husayn's small party, including women and children, was intercepted and forced to camp at Karbala on the Euphrates, where an army of several thousand cut them off from the river. On 10 Muharram 61 AH (10 October 680) Husayn and some seventy men were killed after refusing to surrender; the accounts dwell on the thirst of the besieged and the death of his infant son. The women and his surviving son Ali, later the fourth Shia imam, were taken to Damascus.

Husayn's death became the defining sacrifice of Shia Islam, mourned each year on Ashura, and his shrine at Karbala one of its holiest sites.
story.zh:
680年哈里发穆阿维叶去世，其子叶齐德继位，这是伊斯兰历史上首次世袭继承。阿里之子、穆罕默德外孙侯赛因拒绝效忠，并接受库法支持者的邀请，前去领导他们。但在他抵达之前，倭马亚总督欧拜杜拉·本·齐亚德已镇压了库法的运动。

侯赛因一行人数不多，还有妇女和儿童。他们被拦截，被迫在幼发拉底河畔的卡尔巴拉扎营，数千人的军队切断了他们的水源。伊斯兰历61年穆哈兰姆月10日（680年10月10日），拒绝投降的侯赛因与约七十名男子遇难；史料着力描写被围者的干渴以及他襁褓中幼子的死。妇女们和他幸存的儿子阿里（后来的什叶派第四代伊玛目）被押往大马士革。

侯赛因之死成为什叶派伊斯兰教最具象征意义的牺牲，每年阿舒拉节都要举哀纪念，他在卡尔巴拉的陵墓也成为什叶派最神圣的圣地之一。

summary.en: The Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik completed the Dome of the Rock on the Haram al-Sharif (Temple Mount) in Jerusalem. It is the oldest surviving major Islamic monument; its mosaic inscription is dated 72 AH (691–692).
summary.zh: 倭马亚哈里发阿卜杜勒-马利克在耶路撒冷的尊贵禁地（圣殿山）建成圆顶清真寺。它是现存最古老的大型伊斯兰建筑，其马赛克铭文纪年为希吉拉历72年（691—692年）。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Dome of the Rock
O. Grabar, The Dome of the Rock (2006)

story.en:
The caliph Abd al-Malik built the Dome of the Rock over the outcrop of bedrock on Jerusalem's Temple Mount, the Haram al-Sharif. The rock is linked in Jewish tradition with the Temple and in Muslim tradition with Muhammad's Night Journey and ascension. The mosaic inscription inside the building gives the year 72 AH, corresponding to 691–692.

It is not a mosque but a shrine: an octagon of two ambulatories around the rock, crowned by a gilded wooden dome, in a plan inherited from Byzantine martyria. Inside, gold-ground mosaics of jewelled trees and vines avoid human figures, and a long Arabic band of Qur'anic verses addresses Christians directly, rejecting the idea that God has a son.

Historians debate Abd al-Malik's motives, from rivalry with the Church of the Holy Sepulchre to a civil war that cut off Mecca. Whatever the reason, the building announced that Islam was in Jerusalem to stay, and it remains the city's landmark.
story.zh:
哈里发阿卜杜勒·马利克在耶路撒冷圣殿山（尊贵禁地）的一块基岩之上修建了圆顶清真寺。在犹太传统中，这块岩石与圣殿相关；在穆斯林传统中，则与穆罕默德的夜行登霄相连。建筑内的马赛克铭文标明伊斯兰历72年，相当于公元691至692年。

它并非礼拜用的清真寺，而是一座圣祠：两重回廊环绕岩石构成八角形，上覆镀金木制穹顶，平面布局承袭拜占庭的殉道者纪念堂。内部金底马赛克描绘缀满珠宝的树木与藤蔓，避免人物形象；一条很长的阿拉伯文《古兰经》经文饰带直接向基督徒发言，否认神有儿子之说。

史家对阿卜杜勒·马利克的动机争论不休：或为与圣墓教堂一较高下，或因内战阻断了前往麦加的道路。无论原因为何，这座建筑宣告伊斯兰已扎根耶路撒冷，至今仍是这座城市的地标。

name.zh: 大马士革倭马亚清真寺建成

summary.en: Caliph al-Walid I built the Great Mosque of Damascus on the site of a Roman temple and the church of St John the Baptist. Its mosaics and layout became a model for later congregational mosques.
summary.zh: 哈里发瓦利德一世在罗马神庙和施洗者约翰教堂的旧址上修建大马士革大清真寺。其马赛克装饰和布局成为后世聚礼清真寺的典范。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Great Mosque of Damascus
F. B. Flood, The Great Mosque of Damascus (2001)

summary.en: A movement launched in Khorasan by Abu Muslim in the name of the Prophet's family overthrew the Umayyads. After victory on the Great Zab in 750 the Abbasids took power, shifting the caliphate's centre from Syria to Iraq.
summary.zh: 阿布·穆斯林以先知家族之名在呼罗珊发动起义，推翻倭马亚王朝。750年大扎卜河之战获胜后阿拔斯家族掌权，哈里发国的中心由叙利亚移至伊拉克。

label.zh: 迈尔万二世在埃及被杀

sources.title: al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings, vol. XXVII (trans. Williams)

note: Open revolt began 9 June 747 (25 Ramadan 129 AH); Wikidata gives 746. Point placed at Kufa, where al-Saffah was proclaimed caliph in 749; the revolt itself began near Merv (first route stop).

story.en:
By the 740s Umayyad rule was weakened by tribal feuds, civil war and resentment among non-Arab converts who paid taxes yet were treated as second-class Muslims. In Khorasan, agents of the Abbasid family, descendants of Muhammad's uncle al-Abbas, had spent years preaching for an unnamed "chosen one from the family of the Prophet". In June 747 their organiser Abu Muslim raised the black banners near Merv.

The rebel army swept west, took Kufa, and in 749 the Abbasid Abu al-Abbas was proclaimed caliph there as al-Saffah. In January 750 the last Umayyad caliph, Marwan II, was routed on the Great Zab River; he fled to Egypt and was killed. Many of his relatives were then massacred, though one prince, Abd al-Rahman, escaped to found an Umayyad emirate in Córdoba.

The new dynasty soon discarded allies who had become dangerous: al-Mansur had Abu Muslim murdered in 755. The caliphate's centre moved from Syria to Iraq, where Persian court traditions gained ground.
story.zh:
到740年代，部落仇杀、内战以及非阿拉伯改宗者的怨愤削弱了倭马亚王朝的统治；这些改宗者照样纳税，却被当作二等穆斯林。在呼罗珊，穆罕默德叔父阿拔斯的后裔阿拔斯家族的密使多年来一直以“先知家族中的被选者”为号召秘密宣传。747年6月，组织者艾布·穆斯林在木鹿附近举起黑旗。

起义军一路西进，攻占库法；749年，阿拔斯家族的艾布·阿拔斯在那里被拥立为哈里发，号萨法赫。750年1月，倭马亚末代哈里发马尔万二世在大扎卜河畔惨败，逃往埃及后被杀。随后他的许多亲族遭到屠杀，但王子阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼逃脱，在科尔多瓦建立了倭马亚埃米尔国。

新王朝很快清除了变得危险的盟友：曼苏尔于755年下令杀害艾布·穆斯林。哈里发国的中心从叙利亚移到伊拉克，波斯宫廷传统的影响也日益增强。

summary.en: Caliph al-Mansur founded his round capital, Madinat al-Salam ("City of Peace"), on the west bank of the Tigris. Baghdad grew into the largest city of the Islamic world and a centre of trade, learning and government for five centuries.
summary.zh: 哈里发曼苏尔在底格里斯河西岸兴建圆形新都“和平之城”。巴格达发展为伊斯兰世界最大的城市，五百年间一直是商业、学术和政治中心。

story.en:
The second Abbasid caliph, al-Mansur, wanted a capital away from the restless garrison town of Kufa and close to the Persian heartland. He chose a site on the Tigris near a village called Baghdad, where the river came close to the Euphrates and canals linked the two. Building began in 762; astrologers, including the Persian Nawbakht, are said to have chosen the auspicious day.

The core was a Round City about two kilometres across, with double walls, four gates facing Kufa, Basra, Khorasan and Syria, and at the centre the caliph's green-domed palace and the great mosque. Tens of thousands of workers and craftsmen were brought in to build it.

Markets soon spilled outside the walls, and suburbs grew on both banks. Within decades Baghdad was probably the largest city in the world outside China, a hub for trade from India to the Mediterranean and the home of the translation movement. Almost nothing of the Round City survives today.
story.zh:
阿拔斯王朝第二任哈里发曼苏尔想把都城建在远离动荡军镇库法、又靠近波斯腹地的地方。他选中了底格里斯河畔一个名叫巴格达的村落附近：这里两河相距最近，运河将它们相连。762年动工；据说包括波斯人瑙巴赫特在内的占星家为奠基挑选了吉日。

城市核心是一座直径约两公里的圆城，筑有双重城墙，四座城门分别朝向库法、巴士拉、呼罗珊和叙利亚，中央是哈里发的绿穹宫殿和大清真寺。为修建此城，征调了数以万计的工匠与劳力。

市集很快溢出城墙，郊区在两岸蔓延开来。数十年间，巴格达大概已成为中国以外世界上最大的城市，是从印度到地中海的贸易枢纽和翻译运动的中心。如今圆城几乎没有任何遗迹留存。

summary.en: The Abbasid palace library known as the Bayt al-Hikma became associated with translating Greek, Persian and Indian works into Arabic. Under al-Ma'mun, scholars such as al-Khwarizmi worked in Baghdad, part of a translation movement that underpinned medieval science.
summary.zh: 阿拔斯宫廷图书馆“智慧宫”与把希腊、波斯和印度典籍译成阿拉伯文的事业密切相关。马蒙在位时，花剌子密等学者在巴格达从事研究，这场翻译运动奠定了中世纪科学的基础。

sources.title: D. Gutas, Greek Thought, Arabic Culture (1998)

note: Wikidata gives c. 800 as its start (Harun al-Rashid's library); placed at c. 830, its peak under al-Ma'mun (813–833).

story.en:
The Bayt al-Hikma began as a palace library under the early Abbasids, perhaps modelled on Sasanian royal archives, and grew under Harun al-Rashid and especially his son al-Ma'mun (r. 813–833). Its exact form is debated; some historians see a working academy, others mainly a library and copying office. What is certain is that Baghdad became the centre of an extraordinary effort to translate Greek, Syriac, Persian and Sanskrit works into Arabic.

Wealthy patrons paid handsomely. The Nestorian Christian physician Hunayn ibn Ishaq and his team rendered much of Galen and Aristotle, comparing several manuscripts to fix the text. A later anecdote, probably embellished, says al-Ma'mun paid him the weight in gold of the books he translated.

Al-Khwarizmi and the Banu Musa brothers worked in this milieu, and al-Ma'mun sponsored astronomical observations and an expedition to measure a degree of the meridian. The Arabic texts it produced later passed into Latin and shaped European science.
story.zh:
“智慧宫”起初是阿拔斯王朝早期的宫廷图书馆，或许仿照萨珊王室档案馆而设，在哈伦·拉希德、尤其是其子马蒙（813—833年在位）治下逐渐扩大。它的确切形态尚有争议：有史家认为是一所实际运作的学院，也有人认为主要是图书馆和抄书处。可以确定的是，巴格达成为一项非凡事业的中心：把希腊语、叙利亚语、波斯语和梵语著作译为阿拉伯语。

富有的赞助人出手阔绰。聂斯脱利派基督徒医生侯奈因·伊本·伊斯哈格及其团队翻译了盖伦和亚里士多德的大量著作，并比对多份抄本以校定文本。后世一则大概经过渲染的轶事说，马蒙按他所译书籍的重量付给他黄金。

花拉子米和穆萨三兄弟都活跃于这一环境；马蒙还资助天文观测，并派出测量子午线一度长度的考察队。这里产生的阿拉伯文著作后来被译成拉丁文，深刻影响了欧洲科学。

summary.en: In Tus, Ferdowsi completed the Shahnameh ("Book of Kings"), an epic of some 50,000 couplets recounting Iran's myths and history down to the Arab conquest. Written in Persian with few Arabic loanwords, it became Iran's national epic.
summary.zh: 菲尔多西在图斯完成《列王纪》，以约五万联诗句讲述伊朗从神话时代到阿拉伯征服的历史。全诗以少用阿拉伯借词的波斯语写成，成为伊朗的民族史诗。

note: Wikidata dates the work c. 1000; the final version is dated 1010 in the poem itself.

summary.en: Avicenna (Ibn Sina) completed al-Qanun fi al-Tibb, a five-book synthesis of Greek and Islamic medicine written in Hamadan and Isfahan. Translated into Latin in the 12th century, it remained a standard medical textbook in Europe and the Islamic world for centuries.
summary.zh: 伊本·西那在哈马丹和伊斯法罕写成五卷本《医典》，集希腊与伊斯兰医学之大成。12世纪译为拉丁文后，数百年间一直是欧洲和伊斯兰世界的标准医学教科书。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: The Canon of Medicine

note: Completion date c. 1025 is approximate.

summary.en: The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan routed the Byzantine army near Manzikert, north of Lake Van, and captured Emperor Romanos IV Diogenes. The Byzantine civil strife that followed let Turkish groups settle across Anatolia, beginning its gradual Turkification.
summary.zh: 塞尔柱苏丹阿尔普·阿尔斯兰在凡湖以北的曼齐刻尔特附近大败拜占庭军队，俘虏皇帝罗曼努斯四世。此后拜占庭陷入内乱，突厥部众得以遍布安纳托利亚，开启了该地区逐步突厥化的进程。

sources.title: C. Hillenbrand, Turkish Myth and Muslim Symbol: The Battle of Manzikert (2007)

story.en:
In 1071 the emperor Romanos IV Diogenes led a large but mixed army of Byzantine troops and mercenaries, including Normans, Pechenegs and Oghuz Turks, east to secure Armenia against Turkish raids. The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan, campaigning in Syria, hurried north and offered terms, which Romanos rejected. Part of the Byzantine army had been detached and never rejoined.

On 26 August near Manzikert, north of Lake Van, the Seljuk horse archers fell back before the Byzantine advance. When Romanos turned to withdraw at dusk, the rearguard under Andronikos Doukas, a member of a rival family, marched off the field, and the emperor was surrounded and captured. According to Byzantine and Muslim accounts, Alp Arslan treated him courteously and released him for a ransom and a treaty.

The real disaster came afterwards. Romanos was deposed, blinded and died, and in the civil wars that followed rival factions hired Turkish bands, who settled across Anatolia and soon founded the Sultanate of Rum.
story.zh:
1071年，皇帝罗曼努斯四世·第欧根尼率领一支庞大但成分混杂的军队东征，其中有拜占庭部队，也有诺曼人、佩切涅格人和乌古斯突厥人等雇佣兵，目的是保卫亚美尼亚免遭突厥人侵袭。正在叙利亚作战的塞尔柱苏丹阿尔普·阿尔斯兰急速北上，提出议和条件，遭罗曼努斯拒绝。拜占庭军的一部分已被分派出去，始终没有归队。

8月26日，在凡湖以北的曼齐刻尔特附近，塞尔柱骑射手在拜占庭军推进面前且战且退。黄昏时分罗曼努斯掉头撤军，由敌对家族成员安德罗尼库斯·杜卡斯指挥的后卫竟擅自离开战场，皇帝被包围俘虏。据拜占庭与穆斯林史料记载，阿尔普·阿尔斯兰以礼相待，在获得赎金和条约后将他释放。

真正的灾难随后到来。罗曼努斯被废黜、刺瞎，不久死去。在接踵而至的内战中，各派争相雇用突厥部众，他们在安纳托利亚各地定居，很快建立了罗姆苏丹国。

summary.en: Answering Pope Urban II's appeal, Western European armies marched through Anatolia and Syria, took Nicaea, Antioch and finally Jerusalem, and founded the crusader states of Edessa, Antioch, Jerusalem and later Tripoli.
summary.zh: 响应教皇乌尔班二世的号召，西欧军队穿越安纳托利亚和叙利亚，先后攻占尼西亚、安条克，最终夺取耶路撒冷，建立了埃德萨、安条克、耶路撒冷以及稍后的的黎波里等十字军国家。

sources.title: T. Asbridge, The First Crusade: A New History (2004)

note: Event point placed at Antioch, the crusade's longest siege.

story.en:
In November 1095 at Clermont, Pope Urban II responded to a Byzantine appeal for help against the Turks with a call to free Jerusalem, promising remission of sins. Several princely armies set out in 1096, gathered at Constantinople and, with Byzantine help, took Nicaea in June 1097. They then beat the Seljuks of Rum at Dorylaeum and crossed Anatolia in summer heat, losing many horses and men.

The siege of Antioch, from October 1097 to June 1098, nearly destroyed them. Bohemond of Taranto got inside through a tower guard, and days later the crusaders were themselves besieged by a relief army under Kerbogha of Mosul. During the siege a pilgrim, Peter Bartholomew, claimed visions that led to the finding of a lance said to have pierced Christ; the discovery lifted morale before the crusaders broke out and routed Kerbogha.

The remaining host reached Jerusalem in 1099. The crusade created the Latin states of Edessa, Antioch and Jerusalem; with the County of Tripoli, added in 1109, Latin rule on the coast lasted in shrinking form until 1291.
story.zh:
1095年11月，教宗乌尔班二世在克莱蒙回应拜占庭抵御突厥人的求援，号召解放耶路撒冷，并许诺赦免罪罚。1096年，数支诸侯大军出发，在君士坦丁堡会合，1097年6月在拜占庭协助下攻占尼西亚。随后他们在多利留姆击败罗姆塞尔柱人，在酷暑中穿越安纳托利亚，损失了大量马匹和人员。

1097年10月至1098年6月的安条克之围几乎让十字军覆灭。塔兰托的博希蒙德买通一名塔楼守卫入城，几天后十字军自己又被摩苏尔的克尔博加率领的援军围困。围城期间，朝圣者彼得·巴塞洛缪声称见到异象，人们随之找到一支据称曾刺穿基督的长矛；这一发现鼓舞了士气，十字军随即出城击溃克尔博加。

余下的大军于1099年抵达耶路撒冷。这次十字军东征建立了埃德萨、安条克和耶路撒冷三个拉丁国家；加上1109年建立的的黎波里伯国，拉丁人在沿海的统治在不断萎缩中一直延续到1291年。

summary.en: Crusader forces stormed Jerusalem, then held by the Fatimids, on 15 July 1099 after a five-week siege. The capture was followed by a massacre of many Muslim and Jewish inhabitants, and Godfrey of Bouillon became the first ruler of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.
summary.zh: 经五周围攻，十字军于1099年7月15日攻破法蒂玛王朝控制下的耶路撒冷，随后屠杀了大批穆斯林和犹太居民。布永的戈弗雷成为耶路撒冷王国的首位统治者。

sources.title: Ibn al-Athir, al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh (trans. D. S. Richards)

story.en:
When the crusaders reached Jerusalem on 7 June 1099, their army had shrunk to perhaps 12,000–15,000 fighting men, and the Fatimid governor Iftikhar al-Dawla had poisoned wells and expelled the city's Christians. A first assault failed for lack of ladders. Short of water in the summer heat, the crusaders built siege towers with timber from Genoese ships that had docked at Jaffa, and, according to the chronicles, walked barefoot in procession around the walls.

On 15 July Godfrey of Bouillon's tower reached the northern wall, and the attackers poured in. What followed was a massacre: Latin chroniclers boast of blood in the Temple precinct, and Muslim and Jewish sources record killings in the Aqsa Mosque area and the burning of a synagogue. Modern historians treat the chroniclers' numbers as exaggerated but the slaughter as real.

Godfrey took the title Advocate of the Holy Sepulchre rather than king. His brother Baldwin became the first king of Jerusalem in 1100.
story.zh:
1099年6月7日十字军抵达耶路撒冷时，兵力已缩减到大约一万二千至一万五千名战斗人员；法蒂玛王朝总督伊夫提哈尔·达乌拉在水井中投毒，并把城中的基督徒驱逐出去。首次强攻因云梯不足而失败。盛夏缺水之际，十字军用停靠在雅法的热那亚船只的木料造起攻城塔；据编年史记载，他们还赤足绕城墙列队游行祈祷。

7月15日，布永的戈弗雷的攻城塔靠上北墙，攻城者蜂拥而入。随之而来的是一场屠杀：拉丁编年史家夸耀圣殿区内血流成河，穆斯林和犹太史料则记载了阿克萨清真寺一带的杀戮以及一座犹太会堂被焚。现代史家认为编年史中的数字有所夸大，但屠杀确有其事。

戈弗雷没有称王，而是自称“圣墓守护者”。1100年，他的弟弟鲍德温成为耶路撒冷第一位国王。

summary.en: King David IV "the Builder" of Georgia defeated a large Seljuk-led Muslim coalition at Didgori, west of Tbilisi. The victory allowed him to take Tbilisi in 1122 and opened Georgia's golden age.
summary.zh: 格鲁吉亚“建设者”大卫四世在第比利斯以西的迪德戈里击败塞尔柱人领导的穆斯林联军。此役使他于1122年收复第比利斯，开启了格鲁吉亚的黄金时代。

sources.title: Kartlis Tskhovreba (The Georgian Chronicles): Life of David, King of Kings
D. Rayfield, Edge of Empires: A History of Georgia (2012)

summary.en: Saladin trapped and destroyed the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem near the Horns of Hattin above Lake Tiberias, capturing King Guy of Lusignan. Jerusalem surrendered to him on 2 October, prompting the Third Crusade.
summary.zh: 萨拉丁在太巴列湖上方的哈丁角附近围歼耶路撒冷王国军队，俘虏国王居伊。同年10月2日耶路撒冷向他投降，引发了第三次十字军东征。

sources.title: Baha al-Din Ibn Shaddad, The Rare and Excellent History of Saladin (trans. D. S. Richards)

story.en:
In the summer of 1187 Saladin, now master of both Egypt and Syria, laid siege to Tiberias, where Countess Eschiva, wife of Raymond of Tripoli, held the citadel. The bait worked. Against Raymond's own advice, King Guy of Lusignan led the whole army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem out of the springs of Sephoria and across a dry plateau in the July heat.

By the evening of 3 July the Franks were surrounded and without water. Saladin's men set the dry grass alight, and smoke drifted over the exhausted knights. On 4 July the army broke on the twin hill called the Horns of Hattin and the relic of the True Cross was captured. Saladin's secretary describes how the sultan offered the captive Guy a cooling drink, but killed Reynald of Châtillon with his own hand for attacking Muslim caravans and pilgrims.

With its field army gone, the kingdom collapsed. Jerusalem surrendered on 2 October after Balian of Ibelin negotiated terms, and the shock in Europe launched the Third Crusade.
story.zh:
1187年夏，已同时掌控埃及与叙利亚的萨拉丁围攻太巴列，的黎波里伯爵雷蒙的妻子埃斯基瓦死守城堡。这一诱饵奏效了：吕西尼昂的居伊国王不顾雷蒙本人的劝告，率耶路撒冷王国全军离开塞佛瑞亚的泉水，在七月酷暑中穿越干旱的高原。

7月3日傍晚，法兰克军队已被包围且断水。萨拉丁的士兵点燃枯草，浓烟飘过精疲力竭的骑士。7月4日，十字军在名为“哈丁角”的双峰山丘上崩溃，“真十字架”圣物被俘获。据萨拉丁的秘书记载，苏丹给被俘的居伊递上清凉的饮料，却因沙蒂永的雷纳德劫掠穆斯林商队和朝圣者而亲手将其处死。

野战军覆灭后，王国随之瓦解。在伊贝林的巴利安谈妥条件后，耶路撒冷于10月2日投降；消息震动欧洲，促成了第三次十字军东征。

summary.en: Sent west by his brother, the Great Khan Möngke, Hulagu destroyed the Nizari Ismaili strongholds of Iran, sacked Baghdad and ended the Abbasid caliphate, then invaded Syria. The campaign founded the Ilkhanate and was checked only at Ain Jalut.
summary.zh: 旭烈兀奉其兄蒙哥大汗之命西征，摧毁伊朗的尼扎里伊斯玛仪派堡垒，攻陷巴格达、终结阿拔斯哈里发政权，随后入侵叙利亚。此次西征建立了伊利汗国，直到阿音札鲁特才被遏止。

sources.title: Rashid al-Din, Jami' al-Tawarikh (trans. W. Thackston, 1998)
P. Jackson, The Mongols and the Islamic World (2017)

note: The Wikidata item carries no dates; dates follow Rashid al-Din and modern accounts.

story.en:
In 1253 the Great Khan Möngke sent his younger brother Hulagu west with a large army and orders to subdue the lands as far as Egypt. Moving slowly, with siege engineers recruited from China, Hulagu crossed the Oxus in 1256 and turned first on the Nizari Ismailis. Their imam Rukn al-Din Khurshah surrendered at Maymun-Diz in November that year, and Alamut gave up in December; among the scholars who came over to the Mongols was the astronomer Nasir al-Din al-Tusi.

In February 1258 Baghdad fell and the last Abbasid caliph was put to death. Hulagu then entered Syria, taking Aleppo in January 1260 and receiving the surrender of Damascus. News of Möngke's death in 1259 drew him back east with most of his troops, leaving his general Kitbuqa with a reduced force.

That decision proved fateful: the Mamluks of Egypt destroyed Kitbuqa's army at Ain Jalut in September 1260. Hulagu's conquests nevertheless became the Ilkhanate, a Mongol state that ruled Iran and Iraq until the 1330s.
story.zh:
1253年，大汗蒙哥派其弟旭烈兀率大军西征，命其征服直到埃及的土地。旭烈兀行军缓慢，并带着从中国征调的攻城工匠，1256年渡过阿姆河，首先进攻尼扎里伊斯玛仪派。当年11月，其伊玛目鲁克努丁·忽儿沙在麦门底司堡投降，阿拉穆特堡也于12月归降；归附蒙古人的学者中就有天文学家纳西尔丁·图西。

1258年2月巴格达陷落，阿拔斯王朝末代哈里发被处死。旭烈兀随后进入叙利亚，1260年1月攻克阿勒颇，大马士革也开城投降。1259年蒙哥去世的消息传来，旭烈兀率主力东返，只给大将怯的不花留下一支削弱的部队。

这一决定影响深远：1260年9月，埃及马穆鲁克在阿音札鲁特全歼怯的不花之军。尽管如此，旭烈兀的征服成果仍形成了伊儿汗国，这个蒙古政权统治伊朗与伊拉克直至14世纪30年代。

summary.en: After a short siege, Hulagu's Mongol army took Baghdad, sacked the city and executed the last Abbasid caliph, al-Musta'sim. The fall of the caliphal capital, with great loss of life and of libraries, was long remembered as one of the great catastrophes of Islamic history.
summary.zh: 经短暂围攻，旭烈兀的蒙古军攻陷巴格达，洗劫全城并处死末代阿拔斯哈里发穆斯台绥木。哈里发首都的陷落造成大量人员死亡和典籍损毁，长期被视为伊斯兰历史上的重大浩劫之一。

story.en:
When Hulagu demanded his submission, the caliph al-Musta'sim answered with defiance, trusting in the prestige of an office five centuries old. His army was small and his court divided. Late in January 1258 Mongol forces closed on Baghdad from both banks of the Tigris, battered the eastern walls with siege engines and seized the towers within days.

On 10 February the caliph came out to surrender. The city was then sacked for about a week. Contemporary and later chroniclers give death tolls in the hundreds of thousands; historians treat such figures as exaggerated but agree the slaughter was immense. A later tradition holds that so many books were thrown into the Tigris that its water ran dark with ink. According to several accounts, al-Musta'sim was rolled in a carpet and trampled by horses, in keeping with a Mongol reluctance to shed royal blood.

The Abbasid caliphate in Baghdad was finished. A shadow line of Abbasid caliphs was revived in Cairo by the Mamluks, but Baghdad never regained its place as the capital of the Islamic world.
story.zh:
旭烈兀要求哈里发穆斯台绥木投降，后者却仗着这一延续五百年的职位的威望予以拒绝。他的军队弱小，朝廷内部分裂。1258年1月下旬，蒙古军从底格里斯河两岸逼近巴格达，以攻城器械轰击东城墙，数日内便夺取了城楼。

2月10日，哈里发出城投降。随后城市遭洗劫约一周。当时及后世的编年史家所记死亡人数达数十万，史学家认为这些数字有所夸大，但都承认杀戮极其惨烈。后世传说称，大量书籍被抛入底格里斯河，河水都被墨汁染黑。据多种记载，穆斯台绥木被裹在毯子里遭马匹践踏而死，这与蒙古人忌讳流洒王族之血的习俗相符。

巴格达的阿拔斯哈里发政权就此终结。马穆鲁克后来在开罗扶植了一支名义上的阿拔斯哈里发世系，但巴格达再也未能恢复伊斯兰世界首都的地位。

summary.en: Under Hulagu's patronage, Nasir al-Din al-Tusi founded an observatory and library at Maragheh. Its astronomers compiled the Zij-i Ilkhani tables and developed planetary models closely resembling those later used by Copernicus.
summary.zh: 在旭烈兀资助下，纳西尔丁·图西在马拉盖建立天文台和图书馆。那里的天文学家编成《伊利汗天文表》，并提出与后来哥白尼所用模型极为相似的行星模型。

sources.title: G. Saliba, Islamic Science and the Making of the European Renaissance (2007)
A. Sayılı, The Observatory in Islam (1960)

summary.en: In the Jezreel Valley in Palestine, the Mamluks of Egypt under Qutuz and Baybars defeated a Mongol army left in Syria by Hulagu. It was the first major check to Mongol expansion in the west and secured Mamluk rule over Syria.
summary.zh: 在巴勒斯坦的耶斯列谷，忽都思和拜巴尔斯率领的埃及马穆鲁克军击败了旭烈兀留在叙利亚的蒙古军。这是蒙古西进遭遇的第一次重大挫败，确立了马穆鲁克王朝对叙利亚的统治。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Ayn Jalut
R. Amitai-Preiss, Mongols and Mamluks: The Mamluk–Ilkhanid War, 1260–1281 (1995)

story.en:
In 1260 Hulagu's envoys reached Cairo demanding the surrender of the Mamluk sultan Qutuz. Qutuz had them executed and marched north, gambling that the Mongol army left in Syria after Hulagu's withdrawal was beatable. The Frankish barons of Acre, wary of both sides, allowed the Mamluks to pass through their territory and buy supplies.

On 3 September the two armies met at Ain Jalut, the "Spring of Goliath", in the Jezreel Valley. The Mongol commander Kitbuqa, a Christian of the Naiman people, faced a Mamluk army that most modern estimates put at least as large as his own, its core horsemen themselves largely Turkic former slaves from the steppe. Baybars led the vanguard; the Mamluk line wavered under the first Mongol charge, and Qutuz is said to have rallied it by throwing off his helmet and crying out to his men. Kitbuqa was killed and his army routed.

Weeks later Qutuz was murdered on the road home, and Baybars became sultan. The victory secured Syria for the Mamluks and ended the image of Mongol invincibility in the west.
story.zh:
1260年，旭烈兀的使者抵达开罗，要求马穆鲁克苏丹忽都斯投降。忽都斯将使者处死并挥师北上，赌定旭烈兀撤走后留在叙利亚的蒙古军可以击败。阿卡的法兰克贵族对双方都心存戒备，但仍允许马穆鲁克军穿过其领地并购买补给。

9月3日，两军在耶斯列谷地的阿音札鲁特（意为“歌利亚之泉”）相遇。蒙古统帅怯的不花是乃蛮部的基督徒，面对的马穆鲁克军队据多数现代估计至少与蒙古军规模相当，其核心骑兵本身也多是来自草原的突厥奴隶出身。拜巴尔率领先锋；蒙古人首轮冲锋时马穆鲁克阵线动摇，据记载忽都斯掷下头盔高声呼喊，重新稳住了部众。怯的不花战死，蒙古军溃败。

数周后，忽都斯在归途中遇刺，拜巴尔成为苏丹。这场胜利为马穆鲁克保住了叙利亚，也打破了蒙古军在西方战无不胜的神话。

summary.en: Timur defeated and captured the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I near Ankara. The Ottoman state nearly disintegrated in the civil war that followed (1402–1413), delaying its expansion and the fall of Constantinople by half a century.
summary.zh: 帖木儿在安卡拉附近击败并俘虏奥斯曼苏丹巴耶济德一世。奥斯曼国家在随后的内战（1402—1413年）中几近瓦解，扩张和攻取君士坦丁堡因此推迟了半个世纪。

sources.title: C. Finkel, Osman's Dream: The History of the Ottoman Empire (2005)

story.en:
By 1400 the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I, called Yıldırım ("the Thunderbolt"), had annexed much of Anatolia and was blockading Constantinople. Timur, who had sheltered the Anatolian princes Bayezid had dispossessed, answered his insults by sacking Sivas in 1400 and then marching into central Anatolia.

The armies met near Ankara on 20 July 1402. Timur had diverted the local water supply, and Bayezid's troops fought thirsty in the summer heat. During the battle the Tatar cavalry and the contingents of the conquered beyliks went over to Timur, whose camp held their former lords. Bayezid's Serbian vassals under Stefan Lazarević fought on stubbornly, but the sultan was captured. He died in captivity in 1403; the famous story of the iron cage in which Timur displayed him is widely doubted by historians as a later embellishment.

Timur restored the beyliks and left. Bayezid's sons fought one another for eleven years until Mehmed I reunited the state in 1413, and Byzantium gained half a century of reprieve.
story.zh:
到1400年，被称为“雷霆”的奥斯曼苏丹巴耶济德一世已吞并安纳托利亚大部，并封锁君士坦丁堡。帖木儿收留了被巴耶济德剥夺领地的安纳托利亚诸侯，针对巴耶济德的辱骂，他于1400年洗劫锡瓦斯，随后进军安纳托利亚中部。

1402年7月20日，两军在安卡拉附近交战。帖木儿事先截断了当地水源，巴耶济德的士兵在夏日酷暑中忍渴作战。战斗中，鞑靼骑兵和被征服诸侯国的部队倒向帖木儿，因为他们的旧主正在帖木儿营中。斯特凡·拉扎雷维奇率领的塞尔维亚附庸军顽强苦战，但苏丹还是被俘，并于1403年死于囚中；帖木儿把他关在铁笼中示众的著名故事，多被史家视为后世的附会。

帖木儿恢复诸侯国后便离去。巴耶济德的儿子们彼此争战十一年，直到1413年穆罕默德一世重新统一国家，拜占庭也因此多延续了半个世纪。

summary.en: Mehmed II besieged Trebizond, capital of the last Byzantine successor state, and Emperor David Komnenos surrendered in August 1461. Its fall ended the Empire of Trebizond, founded in 1204, and the last Byzantine rule in Anatolia.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德二世围攻最后一个拜占庭继承国的首都特拉布宗，皇帝大卫·科穆宁于1461年8月投降。特拉比松帝国（建于1204年）随之灭亡，拜占庭在安纳托利亚的统治宣告终结。

sources.title: Kritovoulos, History of Mehmed the Conqueror (trans. C. T. Riggs, 1954)
F. Babinger, Mehmed the Conqueror and His Time (1978)

note: Wikidata starts the siege in September 1460; the 1461 campaign and surrender (15 August 1461) are used for the year.

name.en: Battle of Sharur and the rise of the Safavids
name.zh: 沙鲁尔之战与萨法维王朝兴起

summary.en: Leading Qizilbash Turkmen followers, the teenage Ismail defeated the Aq Qoyunlu at Sharur, entered Tabriz and was proclaimed shah. He made Twelver Shi'ism the state religion, founding the Safavid dynasty that shaped modern Iran.
summary.zh: 少年伊斯玛仪率领红头军土库曼部众在沙鲁尔击败白羊王朝，进入大不里士称沙阿。他定十二伊玛目什叶派为国教，建立了塑造近代伊朗的萨法维王朝。

note: Wikidata dates the battle 17 July 1501; other sources place it a few weeks earlier. Coronation at Tabriz followed in 1501.

story.en:
Ismail was heir to the Safaviyya, a Sufi order based at Ardabil whose Turkmen devotees wore red caps with twelve folds and were nicknamed Qizilbash, "red heads". His father Haydar was killed in battle when Ismail was an infant, and the boy spent years hidden in Gilan before emerging in 1499 to gather his followers.

In 1501, still only about fourteen, he defeated the Aq Qoyunlu ruler Alvand at Sharur, entered Tabriz and was crowned shah. He at once proclaimed Twelver Shi'ism the religion of the realm, although most of his new subjects were Sunni. His devotees regarded him as a figure of near-divine charisma, an image he cultivated in Turkic verse written under the pen name Khata'i.

Within a decade Ismail had conquered most of Iran and defeated the Uzbek Shaybani Khan at Merv in 1510. The Shi'i identity he imposed endured long after the dynasty and remains a defining feature of Iran today.
story.zh:
伊斯迈尔是萨法维教团的继承人。这个以阿尔达比勒为中心的苏非教团，其土库曼信徒头戴有十二道褶的红帽，被称为“奇兹尔巴什”（红头）。伊斯迈尔尚在襁褓时，父亲海达尔战死，他在吉兰藏匿多年，1499年才出山召集追随者。

1501年，年仅约十四岁的伊斯迈尔在沙鲁尔击败白羊王朝统治者阿尔万德，进入大不里士加冕为沙。他随即宣布十二伊玛目什叶派为国教，尽管新臣民大多是逊尼派。信徒视他为近乎神圣的魅力人物，他本人也以笔名“哈塔伊”创作突厥语诗歌，经营这一形象。

不到十年，伊斯迈尔已征服伊朗大部，并于1510年在梅尔夫击败乌兹别克首领昔班尼汗。他所确立的什叶派认同在王朝灭亡后仍长久延续，至今仍是伊朗的鲜明特征。

summary.en: The Ottoman sultan Selim I, with artillery and Janissary firearms, defeated Shah Ismail's Qizilbash cavalry at Chaldiran and briefly occupied Tabriz. The battle set a long-lasting Ottoman–Safavid frontier across eastern Anatolia and Mesopotamia.
summary.zh: 奥斯曼苏丹塞利姆一世凭借火炮和近卫军火器，在查尔迪兰击败伊斯玛仪沙阿的红头军骑兵，并一度占领大不里士。此役确立了横贯安纳托利亚东部和美索不达米亚的奥斯曼—萨法维长期边界。

story.en:
Shah Ismail's preachers had won a large following among the Turkmen tribes of Ottoman Anatolia, and in 1511 a pro-Safavid revolt shook the empire. Selim I, who seized the Ottoman throne in 1512, persecuted suspected Qizilbash sympathisers and in 1514 marched east with a large army, Janissary musketeers and field artillery.

On 23 August 1514 the armies met on the plain of Chaldiran, north-east of Lake Van. The Safavid cavalry charged bravely, but the Ottomans had drawn up their guns behind a barrier of chained carts, and the firepower shattered the attacks. Ismail was wounded and fled; Selim entered Tabriz in early September. His Janissaries, however, refused to winter so far from home, and he withdrew.

Chaldiran gave the Ottomans eastern Anatolia and Diyarbakır and fixed the broad lines of a frontier that later treaties confirmed. According to later Safavid tradition, Ismail never again led an army in person.
story.zh:
沙·伊斯迈尔的传道者在奥斯曼安纳托利亚的土库曼部落中赢得大批追随者，1511年一场亲萨法维的叛乱震撼了帝国。1512年夺得奥斯曼王位的塞利姆一世迫害被怀疑同情红头军的人，并于1514年率大军东征，带着禁卫军火枪手和野战火炮。

1514年8月23日，两军在凡湖东北的查尔迪兰平原交战。萨法维骑兵英勇冲锋，但奥斯曼人把火炮布置在以锁链相连的车阵之后，火力击溃了一波波进攻。伊斯迈尔负伤逃走，塞利姆于9月初进入大不里士。然而禁卫军拒绝在远离家乡之地过冬，他只得撤军。

查尔迪兰之战使奥斯曼获得安纳托利亚东部和迪亚巴克尔，奠定了此后条约所确认的边界大致走向。据后来的萨法维传统记载，伊斯迈尔此后再未亲自统军出征。

name.en: Ottoman–Mamluk War (Ottoman conquest of Syria and Egypt)
name.zh: 奥斯曼-马穆鲁克战争（奥斯曼征服叙利亚与埃及）

summary.en: Selim I turned south after Chaldiran, killing the Mamluk sultan Qansuh al-Ghawri at Marj Dabiq and taking Aleppo, Damascus and Jerusalem, then Cairo in January 1517. The Ottomans gained Syria, Egypt and guardianship of Mecca and Medina.
summary.zh: 查尔迪兰之战后，塞利姆一世挥师南下，在达比格草原击毙马穆鲁克苏丹甘苏赫·古里，夺取阿勒颇、大马士革和耶路撒冷，并于1517年1月攻入开罗。奥斯曼由此获得叙利亚、埃及及麦加和麦地那的守护权。

sources.title: Ibn Iyas, Bada'i al-Zuhur fi Waqa'i al-Duhur

note: Event point at Marj Dabiq (24 August 1516).

story.en:
After Chaldiran, Selim I turned on the Mamluk sultanate, which had sheltered his enemies and was suspected of dealing with the Safavids. On 24 August 1516 he met the aged sultan Qansuh al-Ghawri at Marj Dabiq, north of Aleppo. The governor of Aleppo, Khayr Bey, abandoned the Mamluk wing at the decisive moment, Ottoman guns did their work, and al-Ghawri died on the field.

Aleppo, Damascus and Jerusalem opened their gates. In Cairo the Mamluks chose Tumanbay II as sultan, but Selim crossed Sinai and defeated him at Ridaniya in January 1517. Tumanbay was hanged at Cairo's Bab Zuwayla gate that April. The sharif of Mecca sent his submission, and Selim took the title "Servant of the Two Holy Sanctuaries".

The war brought Syria, Egypt and the Hejaz under Ottoman rule, gave the empire Egypt's revenues and shifted its centre of gravity toward the Arab Muslim lands. A story that the last Abbasid shadow caliph in Cairo formally handed his office to Selim appears only centuries later and is not supported by contemporary sources.
story.zh:
查尔迪兰之战后，塞利姆一世转而进攻马穆鲁克苏丹国，后者曾庇护他的敌人，并被怀疑与萨法维暗中往来。1516年8月24日，他在阿勒颇以北的达比克草原与年迈的苏丹坎苏·高里交战。阿勒颇总督海尔贝伊在关键时刻弃马穆鲁克一翼而去，奥斯曼火炮发挥威力，高里死于战场。

阿勒颇、大马士革和耶路撒冷相继开城。马穆鲁克在开罗拥立图曼贝伊二世为苏丹，但塞利姆穿越西奈，于1517年1月在里达尼亚将其击败。同年4月，图曼贝伊在开罗祖韦拉门被绞死。麦加谢里夫遣使归顺，塞利姆遂取“两圣地之仆”的称号。

这场战争使叙利亚、埃及和汉志归入奥斯曼统治，帝国获得埃及的财赋，其重心也向阿拉伯穆斯林地区偏移。至于开罗末代阿拔斯傀儡哈里发正式把哈里发之位让给塞利姆的说法，几个世纪后才出现，缺乏同时代史料的支持。

summary.en: Suleiman I and Shah Tahmasp I ended four decades of war with the first formal Ottoman–Safavid peace. The Ottomans kept Baghdad, most of Iraq and eastern Anatolia; Iran kept Azerbaijan, and the South Caucasus was divided.
summary.zh: 苏莱曼一世与塔赫玛斯普一世签订首个正式的奥斯曼—萨法维和约，结束了四十年战争。奥斯曼保有巴格达、伊拉克大部和安纳托利亚东部，伊朗保有阿塞拜疆，南高加索被瓜分。

name.zh: 伊斯法罕成为萨法维首都

summary.en: Shah Abbas I moved his capital from Qazvin to Isfahan and rebuilt the city around the vast Naqsh-e Jahan Square with its royal mosque, palace and bazaar. "Isfahan is half the world" became a proverb for its splendour.
summary.zh: 阿拔斯一世将首都从加兹温迁至伊斯法罕，并围绕宏大的伊玛目广场（世界图景广场）兴建王家清真寺、宫殿和巴扎。“伊斯法罕半天下”成为赞美其繁华的谚语。

sources.title: S. Babaie, Isfahan and Its Palaces (2008)

note: Uses the Naqsh-e Jahan Square item; Wikidata dates the square from 1591, while the move of the capital is usually dated 1598.

summary.en: Signed near Qasr-e Shirin, the treaty ended the Ottoman–Safavid war of 1623–1639. Baghdad and Mesopotamia stayed Ottoman, and the Zagros frontier it set roughly anticipates today's Iran–Iraq and Iran–Turkey borders.
summary.zh: 条约在席林堡附近签订，结束了1623—1639年的奥斯曼—萨法维战争。巴格达和美索不达米亚归奥斯曼所有，所定的扎格罗斯边界大致与今日伊朗—伊拉克、伊朗—土耳其边界相当。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Treaty of Qasr-e Shirin

summary.en: Ending the Russo-Persian War of 1826–1828, Qajar Iran ceded the khanates of Erivan and Nakhchivan to Russia, paid a heavy indemnity and granted Russian subjects extraterritorial rights. It fixed the Aras River frontier and marked Iran's loss of the South Caucasus.
summary.zh: 条约结束了1826—1828年俄波战争。卡扎尔伊朗将埃里温和纳希切万两汗国割让给俄国，支付巨额赔款，并给予俄国臣民治外法权。条约确定以阿拉斯河为界，标志伊朗丧失南高加索。

sources.title: F. Kazemzadeh, "Iranian relations with Russia and the Soviet Union, to 1921", Cambridge History of Iran, vol. 7 (1991)

note: Signed 10 February 1828 (Julian; 22 February Gregorian); only the year is given.

summary.en: Protests by merchants, clerics and reformers forced Mozaffar al-Din Shah to accept an elected parliament (Majles) and, in 1906, a constitution, one of the first in Asia. Royalist reaction, civil war and Russian intervention closed the revolutionary period in 1911.
summary.zh: 商人、宗教人士和改革者的抗议迫使穆扎法尔丁沙接受民选议会（马吉利斯），并于1906年颁布宪法，这是亚洲最早的宪法之一。保皇派反扑、内战和俄国干涉使革命时期于1911年结束。

sources.title: E. Abrahamian, Iran Between Two Revolutions (1982)

name.zh: 马斯吉德苏莱曼发现石油

summary.en: Drillers working William Knox D'Arcy's concession struck oil at Masjed Soleyman in Khuzestan, the first commercial oil discovery in the Middle East. It led to the Anglo-Persian Oil Company (later BP) and transformed the region's strategic importance.
summary.zh: 在威廉·诺克斯·达西特许权下作业的钻井队在胡齐斯坦的马斯吉德苏莱曼钻出石油，这是中东首次商业性石油发现。此后成立英波石油公司（后来的BP），该地区的战略地位由此改变。

sources.title: D. Yergin, The Prize: The Epic Quest for Oil, Money, and Power (1991)

story.en:
In 1901 the British financier William Knox D'Arcy bought a sixty-year concession to search for oil across most of Persia from Mozaffar ad-Din Shah. His driller, the engineer George Reynolds, spent years in harsh terrain, and costs mounted until the Burmah Oil Company had to rescue the venture.

By 1908 Burmah's patience was exhausted, and Reynolds was told to wind down. According to the account popularised by Daniel Yergin, the instruction was still on its way when, in the early hours of 26 May 1908, his crew at Masjed Soleyman struck oil at roughly 1,180 feet and a gusher rose above the derrick.

The Anglo-Persian Oil Company was founded in 1909, a pipeline was laid to a new refinery at Abadan, and in 1914 the British government bought a controlling stake to fuel the Royal Navy. The company later became BP. Persian resentment over the terms of the concession grew for decades and culminated in the nationalisation crisis of 1951–53.
story.zh:
1901年，英国金融家威廉·诺克斯·达西从穆扎法尔丁沙手中获得在波斯大部分地区勘探石油的六十年特许权。他的钻井负责人、工程师乔治·雷诺兹在恶劣地形中苦干多年，成本不断攀升，最终只得由缅甸石油公司出资接手。

到1908年，缅甸石油公司失去耐心，通知雷诺兹收尾停工。据丹尼尔·耶金所普及的说法，这一指令尚在途中，1908年5月26日凌晨，雷诺兹的队伍便在马斯吉德苏莱曼约1180英尺深处钻出石油，油柱喷出井架之上。

英波石油公司于1909年成立，并铺设输油管通往阿巴丹的新炼油厂；1914年英国政府购入控股权，为皇家海军提供燃料。该公司后来成为英国石油公司（BP）。伊朗人对特许条件的不满累积数十年，最终在1951至1953年的石油国有化危机中爆发。

summary.en: Officers of the Committee of Union and Progress, starting in Ottoman Macedonia, forced Sultan Abdul Hamid II to restore the 1876 constitution and parliament. The Second Constitutional Era that followed brought the Unionists to power; they later led the empire into World War I.
summary.zh: 统一与进步委员会的军官从奥斯曼马其顿起事，迫使苏丹阿卜杜勒-哈米德二世恢复1876年宪法和议会。随后的第二立宪时期使统一派掌权，他们后来带领帝国加入第一次世界大战。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Young Turk Revolution of 1908

note: Plotted at Salonica (Thessaloniki), the CUP's centre, where the movement began; geographically in Europe.

summary.en: During World War I the Ottoman government of the Committee of Union and Progress carried out the systematic deportation and mass killing of the empire's Armenians, beginning with the arrest of Armenian leaders in Constantinople on 24 April 1915. Scholars estimate 600,000 to 1.5 million deaths; Turkey disputes the term genocide.
summary.zh: 第一次世界大战期间，统一与进步委员会领导的奥斯曼政府对帝国境内的亚美尼亚人实施有组织的驱逐和大规模屠杀，始于1915年4月24日在君士坦丁堡逮捕亚美尼亚知名人士。学者估计死者约60万至150万人；土耳其对“种族灭绝”这一定性持异议。

sources.title: R. G. Suny, "They Can Live in the Desert but Nowhere Else": A History of the Armenian Genocide (2015)
T. Akçam, The Young Turks' Crime against Humanity (2012)

note: Plotted at Deir ez-Zor, destination of the deportation marches; the killings took place across Anatolia and Syria.

story.en:
On the night of 24 April 1915, as Allied forces prepared to land at Gallipoli, Ottoman police in Constantinople arrested more than two hundred Armenian intellectuals and community leaders; most were later killed. In late May a temporary deportation law gave cover to the removal of Armenians from Anatolia, ordered by the ruling Committee of Union and Progress under leaders including Talat Pasha.

Men were often killed outright, and women, children and the elderly were driven in convoys toward the Syrian desert, where many died of starvation, disease and massacre; the camps around Deir ez-Zor became the terminus of the routes in 1916. The US ambassador Henry Morgenthau reported to Washington that a campaign of race extermination was under way.

Scholars estimate between 600,000 and 1.5 million Armenian deaths. The jurist Raphael Lemkin later cited the Armenian case in developing the concept of genocide. Most historians and many states, including the United States since 2021, recognise it as genocide; Turkey acknowledges mass wartime deaths but officially rejects the term.
story.zh:
1915年4月24日夜，正当协约国军队准备登陆加里波利之际，君士坦丁堡的奥斯曼警察逮捕了两百多名亚美尼亚知识分子和社区领袖，其中大多数后来遇害。5月下旬，一项临时驱逐法为将亚美尼亚人迁出安纳托利亚提供了依据，这一行动由执政的团结与进步委员会发动，其领导人包括塔拉特帕夏。

男子常被就地杀害，妇女、儿童和老人则被编队押往叙利亚沙漠，许多人死于饥饿、疾病和屠杀；1916年，代尔祖尔周边的营地成为这些路线的终点。美国大使亨利·摩根索向华盛顿报告说，一场种族灭绝运动正在进行。

学者估计亚美尼亚人死亡人数在六十万至一百五十万之间。法学家拉斐尔·莱姆金后来在提出“种族灭绝”概念时援引了亚美尼亚的案例。大多数历史学家和许多国家（包括2021年以来的美国）承认其为种族灭绝；土耳其承认战时大量死亡，但官方拒绝使用这一称谓。

summary.en: The Allies tried to force the Dardanelles and knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war. After naval attacks failed, British, ANZAC and French landings on the Gallipoli peninsula were contained by Ottoman defenders, among them Mustafa Kemal, and evacuated in January 1916.
summary.zh: 协约国企图强行打通达达尼尔海峡，迫使奥斯曼帝国退出战争。海军进攻失败后，英国、澳新军团和法国部队在加里波利半岛登陆，但被包括穆斯塔法·凯末尔在内的奥斯曼守军遏制，最终于1916年1月撤离。

story.en:
Winston Churchill, First Lord of the Admiralty, hoped that a fleet forcing the Dardanelles could bring Constantinople under its guns and open a sea route to Russia. On 18 March 1915 the Anglo-French squadron ran into an undetected line of mines; three battleships sank and the naval attack was abandoned.

On 25 April British troops landed at Cape Helles, French troops made a diversionary landing at Kum Kale on the Asian shore, and Australian and New Zealand troops came ashore at the cove later named Anzac. On the heights above, the Ottoman lieutenant-colonel Mustafa Kemal threw his 57th Regiment against the invaders, telling them, by his own later account, that he was not ordering them to attack but to die. The regiment was destroyed, but the ridge held, and the campaign settled into trench warfare. A fresh landing at Suvla Bay in August also stalled.

The Allies evacuated in December 1915 and January 1916 without losses. Each side suffered casualties commonly estimated at around a quarter of a million. Gallipoli made Kemal's reputation and became a founding memory for Turkey, Australia and New Zealand.
story.zh:
英国海军大臣温斯顿·丘吉尔希望舰队强行通过达达尼尔海峡，使君士坦丁堡置于炮口之下，并打通通往俄国的海路。1915年3月18日，英法舰队闯入一道未被发现的水雷线，三艘战列舰沉没，海上进攻随即放弃。

4月25日，英军在赫勒斯角登陆，法军在亚洲一侧的库姆卡莱佯攻登陆，澳大利亚和新西兰部队则在后来被称为“澳新湾”的海湾上岸。在其上方的高地，奥斯曼中校穆斯塔法·凯末尔将第57团投入反击；据他本人后来回忆，他对士兵说，他不是命令他们进攻，而是命令他们去死。该团几乎全军覆没，但山脊守住了，战役陷入堑壕战。8月在苏弗拉湾的新登陆同样受阻。

协约国于1915年12月至1916年1月撤离，未遭损失。据通常估计，双方伤亡各约二十五万人。加里波利之战奠定了凯末尔的声望，也成为土耳其、澳大利亚和新西兰的建国记忆。

summary.en: In a secret agreement, British and French diplomats Mark Sykes and François Georges-Picot, with Russian assent, divided the Ottoman Arab provinces into zones of influence. It shaped the post-war mandates and is widely remembered in the region as a symbol of imperial partition.
summary.zh: 英法外交官马克·赛克斯和弗朗索瓦·乔治-皮科在俄国同意下秘密划分奥斯曼帝国阿拉伯诸省的势力范围。协定影响了战后的委任统治格局，在当地被普遍视为帝国主义瓜分的象征。

sources.title: J. Barr, A Line in the Sand (2011)

note: Negotiated in London; plotted at Damascus, at the heart of the territories it divided.

story.en:
While Britain was promising Sharif Husayn of Mecca an Arab kingdom in return for revolt, its diplomat Mark Sykes was negotiating a quite different plan with the French diplomat François Georges-Picot. Concluded in May 1916 with Russian assent, it gave France direct control of coastal Syria, Lebanon and Cilicia, Britain southern Mesopotamia and the ports of Haifa and Acre, and divided the interior into French and British spheres of influence. Palestine was to be under international administration.

Sykes summed up his idea to the British cabinet as a line running from the "e" in Acre to the last "k" in Kirkuk, as James Barr recounts. The deal was secret until the Bolsheviks, having seized power in Russia, published the tsarist government's treaties in November 1917, to the embarrassment of Britain and the anger of its Arab allies.

The agreement was revised many times before the mandates were assigned at San Remo in 1920, but it became a lasting symbol of Western partition of the region.
story.zh:
英国一面向麦加谢里夫侯赛因许诺，以起义换取一个阿拉伯王国，一面又由外交官马克·赛克斯与法国外交官弗朗索瓦·乔治-皮科谈判一个截然不同的方案。该协定于1916年5月在俄国同意下达成：法国直接控制叙利亚沿海、黎巴嫩和奇里乞亚，英国获得美索不达米亚南部及海法、阿卡两港，内陆则划分为英法势力范围，巴勒斯坦拟由国际共管。

据詹姆斯·巴尔记述，赛克斯向英国内阁概括其设想时，说要画一条从阿卡（Acre）的“e”到基尔库克（Kirkuk）最后一个“k”的线。协定原本秘而不宣，直到在俄国夺取政权的布尔什维克于1917年11月公布沙皇政府的条约，令英国难堪，也激怒了其阿拉伯盟友。

在1920年圣雷莫会议分配委任统治地之前，协定已多次修改，但它成为西方瓜分这一地区的持久象征。

summary.en: Sharif Husayn ibn Ali of Mecca, encouraged by Britain, launched a revolt against Ottoman rule in the Hejaz. Arab forces led by his son Faisal, aided by British officers including T. E. Lawrence, advanced north via Aqaba and entered Damascus in October 1918.
summary.zh: 麦加谢里夫侯赛因·本·阿里在英国鼓动下于汉志发动反抗奥斯曼统治的起义。其子费萨尔率领的阿拉伯部队在T. E. 劳伦斯等英国军官协助下经亚喀巴北上，1918年10月进入大马士革。

sources.title: E. Rogan, The Fall of the Ottomans (2015)
T. E. Lawrence, Seven Pillars of Wisdom (1926)

story.en:
In letters exchanged in 1915–16 with Sir Henry McMahon, the British high commissioner in Egypt, Sharif Husayn ibn Ali of Mecca was promised support for Arab independence if he rose against the Ottomans. Tradition holds that Husayn signalled the revolt on 10 June 1916 by firing a rifle from a window of his palace in Mecca. Mecca and Jiddah soon fell, but the Ottoman garrison of Medina under Fakhri Pasha held out until early 1919.

The revolt's army, led by Husayn's son Faisal and advised by British officers including T. E. Lawrence, moved north by raiding the Hejaz Railway. Its boldest stroke came in July 1917, when tribal fighters under Auda abu Tayi crossed the desert and took the port of Aqaba from the landward side, which its defences did not face.

Arab forces entered Damascus in October 1918. Faisal's Syrian kingdom was ended by France in 1920, but he became king of Iraq in 1921 and his brother Abdullah ruled Transjordan.
story.zh:
1915至1916年间，麦加谢里夫侯赛因·本·阿里与英国驻埃及高级专员亨利·麦克马洪往来书信，英方许诺：若他起兵反抗奥斯曼，将支持阿拉伯独立。据传统说法，侯赛因于1916年6月10日从麦加宫殿的窗口开了一枪，作为起义的信号。麦加与吉达很快陷落，但法赫里帕夏率领的麦地那奥斯曼守军一直坚守到1919年初。

起义军由侯赛因之子费萨尔统率，英国军官劳伦斯等人担任顾问，一路袭击汉志铁路向北推进。最大胆的一击发生在1917年7月：奥达·阿布·塔伊率部落战士穿越沙漠，从陆路一侧攻占亚喀巴港，而该港的防御工事原本只面向大海。

1918年10月，阿拉伯军队进入大马士革。费萨尔的叙利亚王国于1920年被法国推翻，但他于1921年成为伊拉克国王，其兄阿卜杜拉则统治外约旦。

name.en: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey

summary.en: After victory in the War of Independence and the Treaty of Lausanne, the Grand National Assembly in Ankara proclaimed the Republic of Turkey, with Mustafa Kemal (Atatürk) as its first president. The caliphate was abolished in 1924 and sweeping secularising reforms followed.
summary.zh: 独立战争胜利和《洛桑条约》签订后，安卡拉的大国民议会宣布成立土耳其共和国，穆斯塔法·凯末尔（阿塔图尔克）任首任总统。1924年哈里发制度被废除，此后推行了全面的世俗化改革。

sources.title: E.-J. Zürcher, Turkey: A Modern History (4th ed., 2017)
Wikipedia: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey

story.en:
By 1923 the nationalist government in Ankara had defeated the Greek army in Anatolia, abolished the Ottoman sultanate (the last sultan, Mehmed VI, left Istanbul on a British warship in November 1922) and won international recognition of Turkey's borders in the Treaty of Lausanne, signed on 24 July 1923.

On 13 October Ankara was named the capital. On the evening of 29 October the Grand National Assembly adopted a constitutional amendment declaring Turkey a republic and that same night elected Mustafa Kemal as its first president; İsmet Pasha (later İnönü) became prime minister the next day. Cannon salutes announced the news across the country.

The caliphate was abolished in March 1924 and the Ottoman dynasty exiled. Over the next decade the republic introduced a civil code based on Swiss law, the Latin alphabet, the Western calendar and women's suffrage, and in 1934 required citizens to take surnames: the assembly gave Kemal the name Atatürk, "father of the Turks". The reforms transformed public life, though they were imposed from above under one-party rule.
story.zh:
到1923年，安卡拉的民族主义政府已在安纳托利亚击败希腊军队，废除了奥斯曼苏丹制（末代苏丹穆罕默德六世于1922年11月乘英国军舰离开伊斯坦布尔），并在1923年7月24日签订的《洛桑条约》中使土耳其的边界获得国际承认。

10月13日，安卡拉被定为首都。10月29日晚，大国民议会通过宪法修正案宣布土耳其为共和国，当晚即选举穆斯塔法·凯末尔为首任总统；次日伊斯梅特帕夏（后姓伊诺努）出任总理。礼炮声向全国宣告了这一消息。

1924年3月哈里发制度被废除，奥斯曼王室被驱逐出境。此后十年间，共和国引入以瑞士法律为蓝本的民法典、拉丁字母、公历以及妇女选举权；1934年又规定公民须采用姓氏，议会授予凯末尔“阿塔图尔克”（意为“土耳其人之父”）之姓。这些改革深刻改变了公共生活，但它们是在一党统治下自上而下推行的。

summary.en: Abdulaziz ibn Saud, who had retaken Riyadh in 1902 and conquered the Hejaz in 1924–25, united his domains as the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The discovery of commercial oil in 1938 later turned it into a leading petroleum producer.
summary.zh: 1902年收复利雅得、1924—1925年征服汉志的阿卜杜勒-阿齐兹·伊本·沙特，将其领地合并为沙特阿拉伯王国。1938年发现商业石油后，王国逐渐成为主要产油国。

sources.title: M. al-Rasheed, A History of Saudi Arabia (2nd ed., 2010)

note: Wikidata dates the unification process 1902–1932; placed here at the proclamation of the kingdom, 23 September 1932.

story.en:
In January 1902 the young Abdulaziz ibn Saud, living in exile in Kuwait, slipped into Riyadh with a few dozen companions and seized the Masmak fortress from the governor installed by the rival Rashidi dynasty. The raid became the founding story of the modern Saudi state.

Over the next quarter-century Ibn Saud expanded from Najd with the help of the Ikhwan, tribal warriors settled in religious colonies. He took al-Hasa in 1913 and Ha'il in 1921, then drove Sharif Husayn's Hashemites from the Hejaz, entering Mecca in 1924 and receiving Jiddah's surrender in December 1925. When the Ikhwan turned against him for refusing to raid British-protected neighbours, he crushed them at Sabilla in 1929.

On 23 September 1932 a royal decree merged his dominions into the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, a date still kept as National Day. The state was poor; a year later it granted an oil concession to Standard Oil of California, whose discovery at Dammam in 1938 transformed the kingdom.
story.zh:
1902年1月，流亡科威特的年轻的阿卜杜勒-阿齐兹·伊本·沙特带着几十名同伴潜入利雅得，从敌对的拉希德家族所派总督手中夺取了穆斯马克堡。这次突袭成为现代沙特国家的建国故事。

此后二十五年间，伊本·沙特借助“伊赫万”（定居于宗教聚落的部落武士）从内志向外扩张：1913年取哈萨，1921年取哈伊勒，随后将谢里夫侯赛因的哈希姆家族逐出汉志，1924年进入麦加，1925年12月接受吉达投降。伊赫万因他拒绝袭击受英国保护的邻国而反叛，1929年被他在萨比拉击溃。

1932年9月23日，一道王室诏令将其领地合并为沙特阿拉伯王国，这一天至今仍是国庆日。当时国家贫穷；一年后它把石油特许权授予加利福尼亚标准石油公司，该公司1938年在达曼的发现彻底改变了王国的命运。

name.en: Discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls

summary.en: Bedouin shepherds found ancient manuscripts in a cave near Qumran by the Dead Sea; by 1956 eleven caves had yielded fragments of hundreds of scrolls. Dating from about the 3rd century BCE to the 1st century CE, they include the oldest known manuscripts of the Hebrew Bible.
summary.zh: 贝都因牧人在死海岸边库姆兰附近的山洞中发现古代手稿；到1956年，十一个洞穴共出土数百部古卷的残片。这些文献约成于公元前3世纪至公元1世纪，包括已知最古老的希伯来圣经抄本。

note: The first cave was found in late 1946 or early 1947.

name.en: Declaration of the State of Israel

summary.en: As the British Mandate ended, David Ben-Gurion proclaimed the State of Israel in Tel Aviv. Neighbouring Arab states intervened the next day; during the 1947–1949 war more than 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled, an event Palestinians call the Nakba ("catastrophe").
summary.zh: 英国委任统治结束之际，戴维·本-古里安在特拉维夫宣布以色列建国。次日周边阿拉伯国家出兵；在1947—1949年战争中，七十多万巴勒斯坦人逃离或被驱逐，巴勒斯坦人称之为“纳克巴”（浩劫）。

sources.title: B. Morris, 1948: A History of the First Arab–Israeli War (2008)

story.en:
On 29 November 1947 the UN General Assembly voted to partition Mandatory Palestine into a Jewish and an Arab state. Jewish leaders accepted the plan; Palestinian Arab leaders and the Arab states rejected it, and fighting between the two communities spread at once.

On the afternoon of Friday 14 May 1948, hours before the British Mandate expired and before the Sabbath began, David Ben-Gurion read the declaration of the State of Israel in the Tel Aviv Museum. The United States recognised the new state within minutes. The next day Egypt, Transjordan, Syria, Iraq and Lebanon sent forces into the former mandate. Armistice agreements in 1949 left Israel holding more territory than the partition plan had allotted it, with Jordan in the West Bank and Egypt in Gaza.

For Palestinians the same events are the Nakba, "the catastrophe": more than 700,000 people fled or were expelled, hundreds of villages were depopulated, and the refugees were not allowed to return. Historians such as Benny Morris have documented both flight and expulsions. In the following years large numbers of Jews from Arab countries also migrated to Israel.
story.zh:
1947年11月29日，联合国大会表决将托管地巴勒斯坦分为一个犹太国和一个阿拉伯国。犹太领导人接受了这一方案；巴勒斯坦阿拉伯领导人和阿拉伯国家则予以拒绝，两大社群之间的冲突随即蔓延。

1948年5月14日星期五下午，在英国委任统治结束、安息日开始前几个小时，戴维·本-古里安在特拉维夫博物馆宣读以色列建国宣言。美国在几分钟内即予承认。次日，埃及、外约旦、叙利亚、伊拉克和黎巴嫩出兵进入原托管地。1949年的停战协定使以色列控制的领土多于分治方案的划分，约旦控制约旦河西岸，埃及控制加沙。

对巴勒斯坦人而言，同一系列事件是“纳克巴”，即“大灾难”：七十多万人逃离或被驱逐，数百个村庄人去村空，难民不被允许返回。本尼·莫里斯等史学家对逃离和驱逐两方面都有记录。此后数年间，大批来自阿拉伯国家的犹太人也移居以色列。

name.zh: 石油输出国组织在巴格达成立

summary.en: At a conference in Baghdad, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela founded the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries to coordinate oil policy. Its power over prices peaked during the oil shocks of the 1970s.
summary.zh: 伊朗、伊拉克、科威特、沙特阿拉伯和委内瑞拉在巴格达会议上成立石油输出国组织，以协调石油政策。其对油价的影响力在1970年代的石油危机中达到顶峰。

summary.en: Iranian army officers and royalists, organised with the help of the US CIA and British intelligence, overthrew Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh, who had nationalised the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company. The coup restored the power of Mohammad Reza Shah and left lasting distrust of the West in Iran.
summary.zh: 在美国中央情报局和英国情报机构协助策划下，伊朗军官和保皇派推翻了将英伊石油公司国有化的首相穆罕默德·摩萨台。政变恢复了穆罕默德-礼萨·沙的权力，并在伊朗留下对西方的长期不信任。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Coup d'etat of 1332 Š./1953

summary.en: Mass protests against Mohammad Reza Shah, uniting clerics, leftists, liberals and bazaar merchants, led to the Shah's departure and Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini's return in February 1979. A referendum then created the Islamic Republic of Iran, led by a clerical Supreme Leader.
summary.zh: 宗教人士、左翼、自由派和巴扎商人共同参与的反对穆罕默德-礼萨·沙的群众运动，迫使国王出走，阿亚图拉鲁霍拉·霍梅尼于1979年2月回国。随后经公民投票建立伊朗伊斯兰共和国，由宗教领袖担任最高领袖。

sources.title: E. Abrahamian, A History of Modern Iran (2008)

story.en:
In January 1978 a government-inspired newspaper article insulting the exiled cleric Ruhollah Khomeini set off protests in Qom. Police shootings led to memorial gatherings forty days later, in keeping with Shi'i mourning custom, and each new round of deaths fed the next. On 8 September, "Black Friday", troops fired on demonstrators in Tehran's Jaleh Square, and strikes by oil workers and bazaar merchants soon paralysed the economy.

Mohammad Reza Shah, ill with cancer and unwilling to order a full crackdown, left Iran on 16 January 1979. On 1 February Khomeini flew back from Paris to a vast welcome. Asked by a journalist on the plane what he felt on returning after fourteen years of exile, he famously answered: "Nothing." On 11 February the army declared its neutrality and the monarchy fell.

A referendum in March approved an Islamic Republic, and a constitution later that year placed a senior jurist, Khomeini himself, at the head of the state. The seizure of the US embassy in November 1979 set Iran's relations with the West for decades.
story.zh:
1978年1月，一篇由政府授意、侮辱流亡教士鲁霍拉·霍梅尼的报纸文章在库姆引发抗议。警察开枪造成死亡，按照什叶派哀悼习俗，四十天后人们举行追悼集会，每一轮新的死亡又引出下一轮抗议。9月8日“黑色星期五”，军队在德黑兰贾莱广场向示威者开枪，此后石油工人和巴扎商人的罢工很快使经济陷于瘫痪。

身患癌症、又不愿下令全面镇压的穆罕默德·礼萨沙于1979年1月16日离开伊朗。2月1日，霍梅尼从巴黎飞回，受到盛大欢迎。在飞机上，有记者问他流亡十四年后归国有何感受，他的回答广为人知：“没有感觉。”2月11日，军队宣布中立，君主制倒台。

3月的全民公决通过建立伊斯兰共和国，同年晚些时候的宪法将一位高级教法学家，即霍梅尼本人，置于国家之首。1979年11月美国大使馆被占领，此后数十年伊朗与西方的关系由此定调。

summary.en: Saddam Hussein's Iraq invaded Iran, hoping to exploit revolutionary turmoil and control the Shatt al-Arab. The war became a costly stalemate with trench warfare, attacks on cities and Iraqi use of chemical weapons; a UN-brokered ceasefire in 1988 left the borders unchanged.
summary.zh: 萨达姆·侯赛因统治的伊拉克企图利用伊朗革命后的动荡控制阿拉伯河而入侵伊朗。战争陷入代价高昂的僵局，伴随堑壕战、对城市的袭击和伊拉克使用化学武器；1988年联合国斡旋停火，边界未变。

note: Plotted at Khorramshahr on the Shatt al-Arab front.

story.en:
Saddam Hussein saw revolutionary Iran as both a threat and an opportunity: its army was purged and in disarray, and he hoped to reverse the 1975 Algiers Agreement on the Shatt al-Arab and perhaps seize oil-rich Khuzestan. Iraqi forces invaded on 22 September 1980 and took the port of Khorramshahr after weeks of street fighting.

The expected quick victory never came. Iran recaptured Khorramshahr in May 1982 and carried the war into Iraq, using massed infantry assaults that included young Basij volunteers. The front hardened into trenches; both sides fired missiles at each other's cities and attacked oil tankers in the Gulf, and Iraq repeatedly used chemical weapons against Iranian troops and against Kurdish civilians at Halabja in 1988.

In July 1988 Iran accepted UN Security Council Resolution 598; Khomeini said doing so was more deadly to him than drinking poison. The ceasefire of 20 August restored the pre-war border. Estimates of the dead range from several hundred thousand to around a million.
story.zh:
萨达姆·侯赛因把革命后的伊朗视为威胁，也视为机会：伊朗军队遭清洗、陷入混乱，他希望推翻1975年关于阜姆河的《阿尔及尔协定》，或许还能夺取盛产石油的胡齐斯坦。1980年9月22日伊拉克军队入侵，经数周巷战攻占港口霍拉姆沙赫尔。

预期中的速胜从未到来。1982年5月伊朗收复霍拉姆沙赫尔，并把战火引入伊拉克境内，发动包括年轻巴斯基志愿者在内的大规模步兵冲锋。战线陷入堑壕对峙；双方用导弹袭击对方城市，在海湾袭击油轮，伊拉克还多次对伊朗军队使用化学武器，并于1988年在哈拉卜贾对库尔德平民施放毒气。

1988年7月，伊朗接受联合国安理会第598号决议；霍梅尼说这对他而言比喝下毒药更致命。8月20日停火，战前边界得以恢复。死亡人数的估计从数十万到约一百万不等。

summary.en: Iraq invaded and annexed Kuwait in August 1990. With UN authorisation, a US-led coalition of some 42 countries began an air campaign in January 1991, and a ground offensive liberated Kuwait by 28 February.
summary.zh: 1990年8月伊拉克入侵并吞并科威特。经联合国授权，美国领导的约42国联军于1991年1月展开空袭，随后的地面攻势于2月28日前解放科威特。

sources.title: L. Freedman & E. Karsh, The Gulf Conflict 1990–1991 (1993)

story.en:
Emerging from the war with Iran heavily in debt, Saddam Hussein accused Kuwait of overproducing oil and of drilling into the shared Rumaila field. On 2 August 1990 Iraqi forces overran Kuwait in a matter of hours and Baghdad soon declared it Iraq's nineteenth province.

The UN Security Council imposed sanctions and in November set a deadline of 15 January 1991 for withdrawal. A US-led coalition assembled in Saudi Arabia, including Arab states such as Egypt and Syria. On 17 January an air campaign began against Iraq; Saddam answered by firing Scud missiles at Israel and Saudi Arabia, hoping to split the coalition, but Israel did not retaliate. The ground offensive launched on 24 February lasted about a hundred hours. Retreating Iraqi troops set hundreds of Kuwaiti oil wells on fire, and the blazes burned for months.

Kuwait was liberated, but Saddam remained in power and crushed Shi'i and Kurdish uprisings that spring. Sanctions, inspections and no-fly zones followed through the 1990s.
story.zh:
与伊朗的战争结束后，债台高筑的萨达姆·侯赛因指责科威特超产石油，并从两国共有的鲁迈拉油田越界开采。1990年8月2日，伊拉克军队在数小时内占领科威特，巴格达随即宣布其为伊拉克第十九个省。

联合国安理会实施制裁，并于11月规定伊拉克须在1991年1月15日前撤军。以美国为首的联军在沙特阿拉伯集结，成员包括埃及、叙利亚等阿拉伯国家。1月17日空袭开始；萨达姆向以色列和沙特发射飞毛腿导弹，企图分化联军，但以色列没有还击。2月24日发起的地面攻势只持续约一百小时。撤退的伊拉克军队点燃了科威特数百口油井，大火燃烧了数月之久。

科威特获得解放，但萨达姆仍然掌权，并在当年春天镇压了什叶派和库尔德人的起义。整个1990年代，制裁、武器核查和禁飞区随之而来。
