summary.en: A US-led coalition invaded Iraq and overthrew Saddam Hussein's government, citing weapons of mass destruction that were never found. The occupation was followed by insurgency and sectarian conflict; US forces withdrew in December 2011.
summary.zh: 美国领导的联军以伊拉克拥有大规模杀伤性武器为由（后证实并未发现）入侵伊拉克，推翻萨达姆·侯赛因政权。占领期间叛乱和教派冲突不断，美军于2011年12月撤出。

sources.title: T. E. Ricks, Fiasco: The American Military Adventure in Iraq (2006)

story.en:
After the attacks of 11 September 2001, the United States and Britain argued that Saddam Hussein's Iraq possessed weapons of mass destruction and could not be contained. Without a new UN resolution authorising force, a US-led coalition invaded on 20 March 2003. Baghdad fell on 9 April, when crowds and US Marines pulled down Saddam's statue in Firdos Square. No stockpiles of such weapons were found.

The Coalition Provisional Authority under Paul Bremer dissolved the Iraqi army and barred senior Baath Party members from public office, leaving hundreds of thousands of armed and embittered men without work. A Sunni insurgency and Shi'i militias grew, and the bombing of the al-Askari shrine in Samarra in February 2006 tipped the country into sectarian civil war. Saddam was captured in December 2003 and hanged in December 2006.

A US troop "surge" and Sunni tribal alliances reduced the violence from 2007, and the last US forces left in December 2011. Estimates of Iraqi deaths vary widely, from over a hundred thousand documented violent civilian deaths to survey-based figures of half a million or more.
story.zh:
2001年“九一一”袭击之后，美国和英国认为萨达姆·侯赛因的伊拉克拥有大规模杀伤性武器，无法加以遏制。在没有联合国新决议授权动武的情况下，美国领导的联军于2003年3月20日入侵。4月9日巴格达陷落，人群与美国海军陆战队在菲尔多斯广场拉倒了萨达姆的雕像。此后并未发现此类武器的库存。

保罗·布雷默领导的联盟驻伊临时管理当局解散伊拉克军队，并禁止复兴党高层成员担任公职，使数十万武装且心怀不满的人失去生计。逊尼派武装叛乱和什叶派民兵日益壮大，2006年2月萨迈拉阿斯卡里清真寺被炸，使伊拉克陷入教派内战。萨达姆于2003年12月被捕，2006年12月被处以绞刑。

2007年起，美军“增兵”与逊尼派部落的结盟使暴力有所下降，最后一批美军于2011年12月撤离。伊拉克死亡人数的估计差异很大，从有记录的十余万平民暴力死亡，到基于抽样调查的五十万甚至更多。

summary.en: Peaceful protests against Bashar al-Assad in 2011 were met with force and escalated into a multi-sided war involving regional and world powers and the Islamic State group. Hundreds of thousands were killed and millions displaced before rebel forces toppled Assad in December 2024.
summary.zh: 2011年反对巴沙尔·阿萨德的和平抗议遭到武力镇压，演变为地区和世界大国及“伊斯兰国”组织卷入的多方战争。数十万人死亡、数百万人流离失所，直至2024年12月反对派武装推翻阿萨德政权。

sources.title: C. Phillips, The Battle for Syria (2016)

note: Point is a generic location in central Syria; the conflict was country-wide.

story.en:
In March 2011, as uprisings spread across the Arab world, security forces in the southern town of Daraa detained and abused teenagers accused of spraying anti-government graffiti. Protests against Bashar al-Assad's government followed and spread nationwide, and the regime answered with live fire and mass arrests. By 2012 army defectors and local militias were fighting back, and the uprising became a war.

The conflict soon drew in outside powers. Iran and Hezbollah backed Assad; Turkey, Gulf states and Western governments supported various rebel groups. In 2014 the Islamic State made Raqqa the capital of its self-declared caliphate, prompting a US-led air campaign allied with Kurdish-led forces. A chemical attack on the Ghouta suburbs of Damascus in August 2013 killed hundreds, and Russian air power from 2015 helped the government retake Aleppo in December 2016.

The front lines then froze for years, until a rebel offensive led by Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham swept from Idlib to Damascus in under two weeks; Assad fled to Moscow on 8 December 2024. The UN human rights office estimated about 307,000 civilian deaths in the first ten years alone; monitoring groups that also count combatants give far higher totals, and about half the pre-war population was displaced.
story.zh:
2011年3月，正当起义浪潮席卷阿拉伯世界之际，南部城镇德拉的安全部队拘押并虐待了被指涂写反政府标语的少年。随后，反对巴沙尔·阿萨德政府的抗议蔓延全国，政权以实弹和大规模逮捕回应。到2012年，军队叛逃者和地方民兵开始武装反击，起义演变为战争。

冲突很快引来外部势力：伊朗和真主党支持阿萨德；土耳其、海湾国家和西方政府支持不同的反对派武装。2014年，“伊斯兰国”把拉卡定为其自封“哈里发国”的首都，引发美国领导、与库尔德人主导的武装合作的空袭行动。2013年8月大马士革郊区古塔遭化学武器袭击，数百人死亡；2015年起俄罗斯空军介入，帮助政府于2016年12月夺回阿勒颇。

此后战线冻结多年，直到“沙姆解放组织”领导的反对派攻势在不到两周内从伊德利卜推进到大马士革；2024年12月8日阿萨德逃往莫斯科。联合国人权事务高级专员办事处估计，仅头十年平民死亡人数就约达30.7万；把战斗人员也计入的监测机构给出的总数要高得多，约一半战前人口流离失所。

summary.en: Two earthquakes of magnitude 7.8 and 7.5 struck south-eastern Turkey and north-western Syria on 6 February 2023, killing more than 50,000 people. Antakya and other historic cities were devastated.
summary.zh: 2023年2月6日，7.8级和7.5级两次地震袭击土耳其东南部和叙利亚西北部，造成五万多人死亡，安塔基亚等历史名城遭到严重破坏。

sources.title: USGS: M 7.8 Pazarcık, Kahramanmaraş earthquake sequence, 6 February 2023

name.zh: 花剌子密著《还原与对消计算概要》

summary.en: In Baghdad al-Khwarizmi wrote a handbook for solving linear and quadratic equations by 'restoring' (al-jabr) and 'balancing', with geometric proofs and practical problems of inheritance and trade. Its title gave algebra its name, and 12th-century Latin translations spread the method in Europe.
summary.zh: 花剌子密在巴格达撰写了一部以“还原”（al-jabr）与“对消”求解一次和二次方程的手册，附有几何证明以及遗产分配和商贸等实际问题。书名成为“代数”一词的来源，12世纪的拉丁文译本将这一方法传入欧洲。

sources.title: MacTutor History of Mathematics: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Musa Al-Khwarizmi
Britannica: The Book of Restoring and Balancing

note: Written under al-Ma'mun (r. 813–833), to whom it is dedicated; c. 820 is a conventional date.

story.en:
Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi, a scholar from Khwarazm working in al-Ma'mun's Baghdad, wrote "The Compendious Book on Calculation by Restoring and Balancing" and dedicated it to the caliph. In its preface he says he meant to teach what people constantly need in inheritance, legacies, lawsuits, trade, land measurement and the digging of canals.

The book has no symbols: everything, even the equations, is written in words. Al-Khwarizmi sorts equations into six standard forms, solves each by rule, and proves the rules for quadratics geometrically by "completing the square" with drawn figures. Al-jabr, "restoring", meant moving a subtracted term to the other side; al-muqabala, "balancing", meant cancelling like terms.

Robert of Chester translated it into Latin in 1145, and al-jabr became "algebra". A separate treatise on Hindu numerals spread decimal place-value arithmetic, and the Latin form of his name, Algoritmi, survives in the word "algorithm".
story.zh:
来自花剌子模、在马蒙时代巴格达工作的学者穆罕默德·伊本·穆萨·花拉子米，撰写了《还原与对消计算概要》，并题献给哈里发。他在序言中说，写作目的是教授人们在遗产分配、遗赠、诉讼、贸易、土地丈量和开挖运河时经常需要的计算方法。

书中没有任何符号，连方程也全用文字表述。花拉子米把方程归为六种标准形式，逐一给出解法规则，并以作图“配方”的方式从几何上证明二次方程的解法。“还原”（al-jabr）指把被减去的项移到等式另一边，“对消”（al-muqabala）指消去两边的同类项。

1145年，切斯特的罗伯特将此书译成拉丁文，al-jabr由此演变为“algebra”（代数）。他另一部关于印度数字的论著传播了十进制位值算术，其名字的拉丁形式Algoritmi则保留在“algorithm”（算法）一词中。

summary.en: Generations of rabbis at the academies of Sura and Pumbedita in Sasanian Mesopotamia debated and expanded the Mishnah; their discussions were redacted into the Babylonian Talmud around 500. It became the central text of rabbinic Judaism, studied and commented on ever since.
summary.zh: 在萨珊波斯治下美索不达米亚的苏拉和蓬贝迪塔经学院，历代拉比对《密西拿》展开辩论和阐发；这些讨论约在500年前后被编订为《巴比伦塔木德》，成为拉比犹太教的核心经典，此后一直被研习和注释。

note: Redaction was gradual (c. 450–550, with later Savoraic editing); 500 is conventional. Marker at Sura.

story.en:
After the Mishnah, the code of Jewish law edited in Galilee around 200, reached Babylonia, the large Jewish community of Mesopotamia made it the core of its study. At academies in Sura and Pumbedita, and in the study circles around them, generations of sages known as Amoraim debated its rulings, adding stories, biblical interpretation, medicine and folklore. They lived under Parthian and then Sasanian rule, led by an exilarch recognised by the Persian kings.

The Talmud preserves arguments as dialogue, often recording rejected opinions beside accepted ones. Tradition names Rav Ashi and Ravina of Sura as its final editors around 500, though anonymous later scholars, the Savoraim, continued to shape the text for generations.

Written in a mix of Hebrew and Jewish Babylonian Aramaic, it outweighed the shorter Jerusalem Talmud, and the Babylonian academies' authority spread across the Jewish world under the caliphs. To this day it is the foundation of rabbinic law and study.
story.zh:
约200年在加利利编定的犹太律法典籍《密释纳》传到巴比伦后，美索不达米亚庞大的犹太社群把它作为研习的核心。在苏拉和蓬贝迪塔的经学院及其周围的研习团体中，世代被称为“阿摩拉”的贤哲辩论其中的裁决，并加入故事、经文诠释、医学和民间传说。他们先后生活在安息和萨珊王朝治下，由波斯国王承认的“流亡者首领”统领。

《塔木德》以对话形式保存辩论，常把未被采纳的意见与被采纳的意见并列记录。传统认为苏拉的拉夫·阿什和拉维纳约在500年完成最终编订，但此后数代被称为“萨博拉”的无名学者仍在继续修订文本。

它以希伯来语和犹太巴比伦阿拉米语混合写成，影响远超篇幅较短的《耶路撒冷塔木德》；在哈里发时代，巴比伦经学院的权威遍及整个犹太世界。时至今日，它仍是拉比律法与经学研习的基础。

name.zh: 巴格达尼扎米亚学院开办

summary.en: The Seljuk vizier Nizam al-Mulk founded a network of endowed colleges teaching Shafi'i law and Ash'ari theology. The Baghdad Nizamiyya, opened in 1067, became the most famous, with al-Ghazali among its teachers, and the endowed madrasa spread across the Islamic world.
summary.zh: 塞尔柱首相尼扎姆·穆尔克创办了一批由宗教基金资助、讲授沙斐仪派法学和艾什尔里派教义的学院。1067年开办的巴格达尼扎米亚学院最为著名，安萨里曾在此任教，这种由基金资助的经学院随后遍及伊斯兰世界。

sources.title: George Makdisi, The Rise of Colleges: Institutions of Learning in Islam and the West (1981)

note: Founded in 457 AH (1065) and inaugurated in Dhu al-Qa'da 459 AH (September 1067); the record marks the opening.

summary.en: A series of strong earthquakes struck northern Syria in October 1138, wrecking the citadel of Aleppo and nearby fortresses such as Harim and Atharib, held by Muslim and Crusader garrisons alike. Chroniclers reported heavy losses; the often-quoted toll of 230,000 rests on a later conflation with other quakes.
summary.zh: 1138年10月，一系列强烈地震袭击叙利亚北部，阿勒颇城堡及哈里姆、阿塔里卜等分别由穆斯林和十字军驻守的要塞遭到严重破坏。编年史家记载伤亡惨重；常被引用的23万死亡人数源于后世与其他地震的混淆。

sources.title: M. Sbeinati, R. Darawcheh & M. Mouty, "The historical earthquakes of Syria: an analysis of large and moderate earthquakes from 1365 B.C. to 1900 A.D.", Annals of Geophysics 48 (2005)
N. N. Ambraseys, Earthquakes in the Mediterranean and Middle East (2009)

note: The 230,000 figure comes from Ibn Taghribirdi (15th c.) and probably merges this event with the 1137 Jazira and 1139 Ganja earthquakes.

summary.en: Built by the Ottoman state largely with donations from Muslims worldwide, the narrow-gauge line from Damascus reached Medina in 1908, cutting the pilgrimage journey from weeks to days. Repeatedly attacked during the Arab Revolt of 1916–18, its southern section was never restored.
summary.zh: 汉志铁路由奥斯曼政府主要依靠世界各地穆斯林的捐款修建，这条窄轨铁路自大马士革南下，1908年通抵麦地那，使朝觐旅程由数周缩短为数日。1916至1918年阿拉伯起义期间屡遭袭击，其南段此后再未恢复。

note: The first train reached Medina on 22 August 1908; the line was formally opened on 1 September 1908, the anniversary of Abdulhamid II's accession. Marker at the Medina terminus.

summary.en: The last stand of the First Jewish–Roman War. Rome’s Tenth Legion built a great ramp against Herod’s cliff-top fortress above the Dead Sea; according to Josephus, the Sicarii defenders took their own lives rather than surrender.
summary.zh: 第一次犹太-罗马战争的最后抵抗。罗马第十军团在死海边希律王的悬崖要塞下筑起巨大坡道；据约瑟夫斯记载，守城的匕首党人宁愿集体自尽也不投降。

note: Josephus’ account is the only narrative source; the date (73 or 74 CE) and the mass suicide are debated by archaeologists.

story.en:
After Jerusalem fell in 70, a band of Jewish rebels known as the Sicarii held out at Masada, a mesa Herod the Great had fortified with palaces and cisterns high above the Dead Sea. In about 73 or 74 the governor Lucius Flavius Silva surrounded it with a wall and camps, still visible from the air, and his troops piled up an earth-and-timber ramp on the western side to bring a battering ram to the walls.

Josephus, the only ancient narrator, says the leader Eleazar ben Yair persuaded the 960 defenders to kill their families and then themselves, and that two women and five children who hid in a cistern told the story to the Romans. Excavations in the 1960s found the ramp, the siege works and a few human remains, but not the mass grave his account implies, so many scholars treat the speech as his own composition.

In the twentieth century Masada became a powerful symbol in Zionist and Israeli memory, though historians continue to debate what really happened there.
story.zh:
70年耶路撒冷陷落后，一群被称为“匕首党”的犹太起义者退守马萨达。这座平顶山岩高踞死海之上，希律王曾在山上修建宫殿和蓄水池。约73或74年，总督卢基乌斯·弗拉维乌斯·席尔瓦用围墙和营地将其团团围住（遗迹至今在空中清晰可见），并在西侧堆起土木坡道，把攻城槌推到城下。

唯一的古代叙述者约瑟夫斯说，首领以利亚撒·本·雅伊尔说服960名守城者先杀死家人再自尽，只有藏在蓄水池里的两名妇女和五个孩子向罗马人讲述了经过。1960年代的发掘找到了坡道、围城工事和少量遗骸，却没有发现其叙述所暗示的大规模墓葬，因此许多学者认为那篇演说是约瑟夫斯自己的创作。

二十世纪，马萨达成为锡安主义和以色列集体记忆中的有力象征，但历史学家对当年究竟发生了什么仍有争论。

summary.en: On the death of King Rabbel II, Trajan’s governor of Syria occupied the Nabataean kingdom and made it the province of Arabia (later called Arabia Petraea); the governor and legion were based at Bostra, while Petra kept the title of metropolis. Trajan then built the Via Nova Traiana from Bostra to the Red Sea at Aila.
summary.zh: 纳巴泰国王拉贝尔二世去世后，图拉真的叙利亚总督占领纳巴泰王国，设立阿拉伯行省（后称阿拉伯佩特拉）；总督和军团驻波斯特拉，佩特拉仍保有“首府”称号。图拉真随后修建了从波斯特拉通往红海艾拉的“图拉真新路”。

summary.en: Trajan annexed Armenia, took the Parthian capital Ctesiphon in 116 and reached the Persian Gulf, the furthest east any Roman emperor marched. Revolts and a failed siege of Hatra followed, and his successor Hadrian gave up Mesopotamia.
summary.zh: 图拉真吞并亚美尼亚，116年攻占安息首都泰西封并抵达波斯湾，这是罗马皇帝向东推进的最远处。随后各地起义、哈特拉久攻不下，继任者哈德良放弃了美索不达米亚。

name.zh: 奥勒良在埃梅萨击败芝诺比娅

summary.en: Having beaten the Palmyrene army at Immae, the emperor Aurelian routed it again outside Emesa (Homs). Zenobia fled to Palmyra and was captured trying to reach the Euphrates; when the city rebelled in 273 Aurelian’s troops sacked it.
summary.zh: 皇帝奥勒良在伊梅击败帕尔米拉军后，又在埃梅萨（霍姆斯）城外将其击溃。芝诺比娅逃回帕尔米拉，在设法渡过幼发拉底河时被俘；273年该城再度起事，奥勒良的军队将其洗劫。

sources.title: R. Stoneman, Palmyra and Its Empire: Zenobia's Revolt against Rome (1992)

note: The sequence Immae–Emesa–Palmyra follows Zosimus; Zenobia’s fate after Aurelian’s triumph is told differently by ancient writers.

story.en:
In the 260s, while Rome reeled from the capture of Valerian, the Palmyrene prince Odaenathus defended the east, and after his murder his widow Zenobia ruled for their young son Vaballathus. By 270 her armies had taken Egypt and much of Anatolia, and in 271–272 her mints struck coins naming her Augusta, an open break with Rome.

Aurelian marched east in 272. At Immae near Antioch his cavalry feigned flight until the heavily armoured Palmyrene horsemen tired, then turned on them; a second battle outside Emesa ended the same way. Zenobia retreated across the desert to Palmyra, and when it was besieged she slipped out on a camel, according to Zosimus, only to be caught at the Euphrates.

Palmyra surrendered, rebelled again in 273 and was sacked. Ancient writers disagree about Zenobia's end: some say she died on the way to Rome, others that she walked in golden chains in Aurelian's triumph and lived out her life in a villa near Tibur.
story.zh:
260年代，罗马因瓦勒良被俘而陷入危机，帕尔米拉王公奥登纳图斯保卫了东方；他遇刺后，遗孀芝诺比娅以幼子瓦巴拉图斯的名义执政。到270年，她的军队已占领埃及和安纳托利亚大部；271至272年间，她的铸币厂发行自称“奥古斯塔”的钱币，公开与罗马决裂。

272年奥勒良东征。在安条克附近的伊梅，他的骑兵佯装败退，待帕尔米拉重甲骑兵疲惫后回身反击；埃梅萨城外的第二场战役结局相同。芝诺比娅穿越沙漠退回帕尔米拉。据佐西莫斯记载，城被围后她骑骆驼出逃，却在幼发拉底河边被擒。

帕尔米拉投降，273年再度反叛，遭到洗劫。古代作家对芝诺比娅的结局说法不一：有人说她死于前往罗马途中，也有人说她戴着金链走在奥勒良的凯旋式中，后来在提布尔附近的别墅终老。

name.zh: 摩尼开始传教（摩尼教兴起）

summary.en: After a second revelation at about 24, Mani left his baptist community in Babylonia and proclaimed a new universal religion. Shapur I received him at court; Manichaeism spread along trade routes to Rome, Central Asia and Tang China before being persecuted almost everywhere.
summary.zh: 约24岁时摩尼获得第二次启示，离开巴比伦尼亚的浸礼派团体，宣讲新的普世宗教。沙普尔一世在宫廷接见了他；摩尼教沿商路传到罗马、中亚和唐代中国，后来几乎在各地都遭到迫害。

sources.title: The Cologne Mani Codex (ed. Koenen & Römer, 1988)
S. N. C. Lieu, Manichaeism in the Later Roman Empire and Medieval China (1992)

note: The date 240 follows the Cologne Mani Codex; Manichaean sources date his first public preaching to 240 or 241.

name.zh: 卡特利（伊比利亚）皈依基督教

summary.en: King Mirian III of Iberia and his court converted, according to Georgian tradition through the preaching of a captive woman, St Nino. Christianity became the royal religion of eastern Georgia, which kept it through centuries of Persian, Arab and Turkish rule.
summary.zh: 伊比利亚国王米里安三世及其宫廷皈依基督教，据格鲁吉亚传统，这要归功于一位被俘女子圣尼诺的布道。基督教成为东格鲁吉亚的王室宗教，此后历经波斯、阿拉伯和突厥统治而延续不绝。

sources.title: S. H. Rapp, Studies in Medieval Georgian Historiography (2003)

note: Usually dated to the 330s (often 326 or 337); the Nino story comes from Rufinus and later Georgian hagiography.

summary.en: The emperor Julian led an army usually estimated at 65,000 or more down the Euphrates to Ctesiphon but could not take it. Retreating up the Tigris he was mortally wounded in a skirmish; his successor Jovian bought peace by ceding Nisibis and five provinces to Shapur II.
summary.zh: 皇帝尤利安率一支通常估计不少于六万五千人的大军沿幼发拉底河南下至泰西封，却未能攻克。沿底格里斯河撤退途中，他在一次遭遇战中受了致命伤；继任者约维安割让尼西比斯和五个行省给沙普尔二世以换取和平。

label.zh: 沿幼发拉底河经过基尔克西乌姆

label.en: Julian mortally wounded on the retreat (26 June)
label.zh: 撤退途中尤利安受致命伤（6月26日）

name.zh: 亚美尼亚分治（阿基里塞内和约）

summary.en: Rome and Sasanian Persia divided the kingdom of Armenia between client kings, Persia taking about four-fifths in the east. The Arsacid monarchy in Persian Armenia was abolished in 428.
summary.zh: 罗马与萨珊波斯在各自扶植的附庸国王之间瓜分亚美尼亚王国，波斯取得东部约五分之四的领土。波斯亚美尼亚的阿萨息斯王朝于428年被废除。

sources.title: R. G. Hovannisian (ed.), The Armenian People from Ancient to Modern Times, vol. 1 (1997)
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Armenia and Iran ii. The pre-Islamic period

note: Dated 384 or 387; the treaty text does not survive.

summary.en: Armenian nobles led by Vardan Mamikonian fought a much larger Sasanian army that had come to impose Zoroastrianism. Vardan was killed and the Armenians lost, but continued resistance won recognition of their Christian faith in the Treaty of Nvarsak (484).
summary.zh: 瓦尔丹·马米科尼扬率领亚美尼亚贵族迎战前来强推琐罗亚斯德教的萨珊大军。瓦尔丹战死，亚美尼亚人战败，但持续的抵抗最终在484年《努瓦尔萨克条约》中为其基督教信仰赢得承认。

sources.title: Elishe, History of Vardan and the Armenian War (5th century)

story.en:
In the 440s the Sasanian king Yazdegerd II tried to bind Armenia more closely to Iran by ordering its nobility to embrace Zoroastrianism. Some lords complied; many, led by the sparapet (commander) Vardan Mamikonian, rose in revolt, and the church preached resistance.

On 26 May 451 the two armies met on the plain of Avarayr, in what is now north-western Iran. The Persians brought war elephants and far greater numbers, and part of the Armenian nobility had gone over to them. Vardan and eight other commanders fell, and the revolt was crushed. The clerical historian Elishe, writing soon after, turned the defeat into a martyrdom, and the Armenian Church honours Vardan and his companions as saints on the feast of Vardanants.

Guerrilla resistance continued for a generation under Vardan's nephew Vahan. In 484 the Treaty of Nvarsak allowed the Armenians to practise Christianity freely, which is why Avarayr is remembered as a defeat that won the war.
story.zh:
440年代，萨珊国王伊嗣俟二世为使亚美尼亚更紧密地依附伊朗，下令其贵族改信琐罗亚斯德教。一些领主顺从了，更多人则在总司令瓦尔丹·马米科尼扬的带领下起兵，教会也号召抵抗。

451年5月26日，两军在今伊朗西北部的阿瓦拉尔平原交锋。波斯人带来战象，兵力远胜对手，而且一部分亚美尼亚贵族已倒向他们。瓦尔丹与另外八名将领阵亡，起义被镇压。不久之后，教士史家叶利舍把这场失败写成了殉道，亚美尼亚教会在“瓦尔达南茨节”尊瓦尔丹及其同伴为圣徒。

在瓦尔丹之侄瓦汉的领导下，游击抵抗延续了一代人之久。484年《努瓦尔萨克条约》允许亚美尼亚人自由信奉基督教，因此阿瓦拉尔被铭记为“输了战役却赢了战争”。

note: Plotted near Churs (Chors), West Azerbaijan, on the Avarayr plain. Usually dated 26 May 451; Iranica gives 2 June (Pentecost).

name.en: School of Edessa moves to Nisibis
name.zh: 埃德萨学派迁往尼西比斯

summary.en: When the emperor Zeno closed the "School of the Persians" at Edessa for its Nestorian teaching, its masters crossed the border to Nisibis in Persia. The School of Nisibis became the intellectual centre of the Church of the East, translating Greek learning into Syriac.
summary.zh: 皇帝芝诺因埃德萨“波斯人学校”传授聂斯托利派教义而将其关闭，学者们越过边境迁到波斯境内的尼西比斯。尼西比斯学院成为东方教会的学术中心，把希腊学问译成叙利亚文。

sources.title: A. H. Becker, Fear of God and the Beginning of Wisdom: The School of Nisibis (2006)

note: Narsai had moved to Nisibis earlier (c. 471); 489 is the year Zeno closed the Edessa school.

name.en: Massacre of the Christians of Najran

summary.en: The Himyarite king Yusuf As'ar (Dhu Nuwas), a convert to Judaism, besieged Christian Najran and executed many who refused to renounce their faith. The killings provoked an Aksumite invasion backed by Byzantium that ended the Himyarite kingdom around 525.
summary.zh: 皈依犹太教的希木叶尔国王优素福·阿萨尔（祖·努瓦斯）围攻信奉基督教的纳季兰，处死许多拒绝弃教的人。屠杀激起拜占庭支持下的阿克苏姆入侵，约525年希木叶尔王国灭亡。

sources.title: The Book of the Himyarites (Syriac, 6th century)
C. J. Robin, "Himyar, Aksum, and Arabia Deserta in Late Antiquity" (2015)

note: Dated 523 (some sources 518 or 520); the death toll in the martyr texts is unreliable.

story.en:
In the early sixth century South Arabia was a battleground of faiths and empires. The Himyarite kings had long favoured a Jewish-leaning monotheism, while the oasis town of Najran had a strong Christian community linked to the Aksumite kingdom across the Red Sea and to Byzantium.

Around 523 the Himyarite ruler Yusuf As'ar Yath'ar, remembered in Arabic tradition as Dhu Nuwas, attacked the Aksumite garrison and then besieged Najran. Himyarite inscriptions of his commanders boast of the dead and captives they took. Syriac letters and the later Book of the Himyarites describe the execution of Christians led by the notable al-Harith (Arethas), and the church came to venerate them as the Martyrs of Najran.

The news travelled to Constantinople and Aksum. With Byzantine encouragement King Kaleb of Aksum crossed the sea around 525, defeated and killed Yusuf, and installed Christian rulers. Abraha, a commander who soon overthrew the first of them, later built a great church at Sana'a and, according to Muslim tradition, marched on Mecca in the "Year of the Elephant".
story.zh:
六世纪初，南阿拉伯是多种信仰和帝国角逐之地。希木叶尔诸王长期偏向犹太教式的一神信仰，而绿洲城镇纳季兰则有一个强大的基督教社团，与红海对岸的阿克苏姆王国及拜占庭联系紧密。

约523年，阿拉伯传统中称为“祖·努瓦斯”的希木叶尔统治者优素福·阿萨尔·亚萨尔袭击阿克苏姆驻军，随后围攻纳季兰。其部将的希木叶尔铭文夸耀杀死和俘获的人数。叙利亚文书信和稍后的《希木叶尔人之书》描述了以显贵哈里斯（阿雷塔斯）为首的基督徒被处死的经过，教会后来尊他们为“纳季兰殉道者”。

消息传到君士坦丁堡和阿克苏姆。在拜占庭的鼓励下，阿克苏姆国王卡莱布约于525年渡海出征，击败并杀死优素福，扶植基督徒统治者。不久推翻其中首任统治者的将领阿布拉哈，后来在萨那修建大教堂，据穆斯林传统，他还在“象年”进军麦加。

name.en: Final breach of the Marib Dam

summary.en: The great dam of Marib, which had irrigated the Sabaean heartland for over a millennium, burst for the last time in the later sixth century after repeated repairs. Arabic tradition (and the Qur'an's "flood of al-Arim") links the disaster to the dispersal of South Arabian tribes northward.
summary.zh: 马里卜大坝灌溉萨巴腹地已逾千年，屡经修缮后于六世纪后期最后一次溃决。阿拉伯传统（以及《古兰经》中的“阿里姆洪水”）将这场灾难与南阿拉伯部落北迁联系在一起。

note: Inscriptions record breaches and repairs in 449/450 and 548 (under Abraha); the final collapse is dated only roughly to c. 570–600.

summary.en: A confederacy of Quraysh and allied tribes, perhaps 10,000 strong, besieged Medina. On the advice, according to tradition, of the Persian convert Salman, Muhammad had a trench dug across the open northern approach; after weeks the coalition broke up, and Mecca never attacked Medina again.
summary.zh: 古莱什人及其盟友部落组成约一万人的联军围攻麦地那。据传统记载，穆罕默德采纳波斯皈依者萨尔曼的建议，在北面开阔的通道上挖掘壕沟；数周后联军瓦解，麦加此后再未进攻麦地那。

sources.title: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (trans. A. Guillaume, 1955)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of the Trench

note: Numbers and the Salman story are traditional.

summary.en: After Muhammad’s death many Arabian tribes stopped paying the alms tax and rival prophets arose. Caliph Abu Bakr’s generals, above all Khalid ibn al-Walid, defeated them, culminating in the bloody battle of al-Yamama against Musaylima, and brought all Arabia under Medina.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德去世后，许多阿拉伯部落拒交天课，各地还出现了自称先知者。哈里发阿布·伯克尔的将领，尤其是哈立德·本·瓦利德，逐一将他们击败，最终在叶麻麦与穆赛利玛进行了一场血战，使全阿拉伯归于麦地那统治之下。

sources.title: E. Shoufani, Al-Riddah and the Muslim Conquest of Arabia (1973)

summary.en: Caliph Ali met Mu'awiya, governor of Syria, on the Euphrates near Raqqa. When Ali’s army seemed to be winning, Syrian troops raised Qur'an pages on their lances to demand arbitration; Ali accepted, a group of his followers seceded as the Kharijites, and the arbitration weakened his claim.
summary.zh: 哈里发阿里与叙利亚总督穆阿维叶在拉卡附近的幼发拉底河畔交战。阿里军队似将获胜时，叙利亚士兵把《古兰经》书页挑在长矛上要求仲裁；阿里接受，部分追随者因此出走，成为哈瓦利吉派，仲裁结果也削弱了阿里的地位。

sources.title: W. Madelung, The Succession to Muhammad (1997)

story.en:
The murder of the caliph Uthman in 656 split the young Muslim community. Ali, the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law, was acclaimed caliph in Medina, but Uthman's kinsman Mu'awiya, the long-serving governor of Syria, refused to recognise him until the killers were punished.

In the summer of 657 their armies faced each other at Siffin on the Euphrates. After weeks of skirmishes and negotiation, a full battle broke out. According to the accounts collected by later historians such as al-Tabari, when Ali's side gained the upper hand, the Syrians, on the advice of Amr ibn al-As, fixed leaves of the Qur'an to their spear points and called for the dispute to be judged by God's book.

Ali agreed to arbitration, which proved disastrous for him. Some of his own soldiers rejected it, saying "judgement belongs to God alone", and broke away as the Kharijites. The arbitrators reached no clear verdict, Ali was murdered by a Kharijite in 661, and Mu'awiya founded the Umayyad caliphate. The divisions of this First Fitna still shape the Sunni–Shi'i split.
story.zh:
656年哈里发奥斯曼遇刺，使年轻的穆斯林社团陷入分裂。先知的堂弟兼女婿阿里在麦地那被拥立为哈里发，而奥斯曼的族人、长期担任叙利亚总督的穆阿维叶则坚持先惩办凶手，拒不承认阿里。

657年夏，双方军队在幼发拉底河畔的隋芬对峙。数周的小规模冲突和谈判之后，大战爆发。据塔巴里等后世史家汇集的记载，阿里一方占上风时，叙利亚人听从阿慕尔·本·阿斯的建议，把《古兰经》书页系在矛尖上，要求以真主的经典裁决争端。

阿里同意仲裁，结果对他极为不利。他的部分士兵反对，喊出“裁决只归真主”，脱离而去，成为哈瓦利吉派。仲裁者未能作出明确裁定，661年阿里被一名哈瓦利吉派刺杀，穆阿维叶建立倭马亚哈里发国。这场“第一次内战”造成的分裂至今仍影响着逊尼派与什叶派的分野。

summary.en: From his mountain fortress of Badhdh in Azerbaijan, Babak led the Khurramite movement, a religious and social revolt against Abbasid rule, for over twenty years. The caliph al-Mu'tasim’s general Afshin finally took the fortress in 837, and Babak, handed over by an Armenian prince, was executed at Samarra in 838.
summary.zh: 巴贝克以阿塞拜疆山中的巴兹堡为据点，领导胡拉米教派的宗教与社会起义反抗阿拔斯统治，历时二十余年。837年哈里发穆阿台绥姆的将领阿夫辛终于攻克要塞，巴贝克被一位亚美尼亚王公交出，838年在萨迈拉被处死。

name.zh: 萨迈拉成为阿拔斯首都

summary.en: Caliph al-Mu'tasim moved his court and Turkish slave guards from Baghdad to a vast new palace-city at Samarra on the Tigris. It remained the capital until 892; its Great Mosque with the spiral Malwiya minaret, added by al-Mutawakkil in 848–851, was then the largest mosque in the world.
summary.zh: 哈里发穆阿台绥姆把宫廷和突厥奴隶禁军从巴格达迁到底格里斯河畔新建的巨大宫城萨迈拉。萨迈拉一直是首都，直到892年；穆塔瓦基勒于848至851年修建的带螺旋形“马尔维亚”宣礼塔的大清真寺，是当时世界上最大的清真寺。

sources.title: A. Northedge, The Historical Topography of Samarra (2005)
UNESCO World Heritage: Samarra Archaeological City

summary.en: East African slaves forced to clear salt flats near Basra rose under the leader Ali ibn Muhammad. For fourteen years they held the marshes of lower Iraq from their capital al-Mukhtara and sacked Basra in 871, until the regent al-Muwaffaq crushed them.
summary.zh: 在巴士拉附近被迫清理盐碱地的东非奴隶在阿里·本·穆罕默德领导下起义。他们以穆赫塔拉为都，盘踞下伊拉克沼泽地区十四年，871年洗劫巴士拉，直到摄政穆瓦法格将其镇压。

sources.title: A. Popovic, The Revolt of African Slaves in Iraq in the 3rd/9th Century (1999)

summary.en: The Qarmatians of Bahrayn, an Ismaili-inspired movement in eastern Arabia, fell on Mecca during the pilgrimage, killed many pilgrims and carried off the Black Stone of the Kaaba. It was returned only in about 951.
summary.zh: 东阿拉伯巴林的卡尔马特派（受伊斯玛仪派影响的运动）在朝觐期间袭击麦加，杀死许多朝觐者，并劫走克尔白的黑石，直到约951年才归还。

name.en: Destruction of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre

summary.en: The Fatimid caliph al-Hakim ordered the church built over the traditional tomb of Jesus to be demolished. It was rebuilt in reduced form under Byzantine patronage in the 1030s–40s, and the destruction was later cited in Latin Europe as a grievance behind the crusades.
summary.zh: 法蒂玛哈里发哈基姆下令拆毁建于传统所称耶稣墓上的教堂。1030–1040年代在拜占庭资助下以较小规模重建，此次破坏后来被拉丁欧洲列为发动十字军的理由之一。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Church of the Holy Sepulchre
M. Biddle, The Tomb of Christ (1999)
Wikipedia: Church of the Holy Sepulchre

summary.en: Sultan Alp Arslan took the former Bagratid capital Ani, then in Byzantine hands, after a siege; contemporaries describe a massacre. The fall of the "city of 1,001 churches" opened Armenia to Turkish settlement seven years before Manzikert.
summary.zh: 苏丹阿尔普·阿尔斯兰经围攻夺取当时属于拜占庭的前巴格拉图尼王朝首都阿尼，同时代人记载了城中的屠杀。“千零一座教堂之城”的陷落使亚美尼亚向突厥移民敞开，这比曼齐刻尔特之战早了七年。

summary.en: Imad al-Din Zengi, atabeg of Mosul, took Edessa after a four-week siege while its count was away, destroying the first crusader state. The shock in Europe prompted Pope Eugenius III to call the Second Crusade.
summary.zh: 摩苏尔阿塔贝格伊马德丁·赞吉趁伯爵不在城中，经四周围攻攻陷埃德萨，消灭了第一个十字军国家。消息震动欧洲，教皇尤金三世由此号召第二次十字军东征。

sources.title: C. Hillenbrand, The Crusades: Islamic Perspectives (1999)

story.en:
Edessa, the old Syriac Christian city east of the upper Euphrates, had been the first crusader conquest: Baldwin of Boulogne made himself its count in 1098, even before Jerusalem fell. By the 1140s the county was exposed and divided, and Count Joscelin II was often away at Turbessel, west of the river.

In late November 1144 Zengi, the Turkish atabeg of Mosul and Aleppo, struck while Joscelin was absent. His engineers mined under the walls and on 24 December a section collapsed; the troops poured in. Contemporary Syriac and Armenian chroniclers describe killing and enslavement, but also that Zengi then halted the slaughter and allowed the native Christians to stay, wanting the city to prosper under him.

The fall of Edessa made Zengi a hero of jihad and shocked Latin Europe. Pope Eugenius III issued the bull Quantum praedecessores and Bernard of Clairvaux preached the Second Crusade, whose failure before Damascus in 1148 only strengthened Zengi's son Nur al-Din.
story.zh:
埃德萨是幼发拉底河上游以东历史悠久的叙利亚基督教城市，也是十字军的第一个征服地：1098年，甚至在耶路撒冷陷落之前，布洛涅的鲍德温就自立为埃德萨伯爵。到1140年代，伯国四面受敌、内部分裂，伯爵约瑟林二世常驻河西的图尔贝塞尔。

1144年11月下旬，摩苏尔和阿勒颇的突厥阿塔贝格赞吉趁约瑟林不在发动进攻。他的工兵在城墙下挖掘坑道，12月24日一段城墙坍塌，大军涌入城中。同时代的叙利亚和亚美尼亚编年史记载了屠杀和掳掠，但也说赞吉随后下令停止杀戮，允许本地基督徒留居，希望城市在其治下繁荣。

埃德萨的陷落使赞吉成为圣战英雄，也震动了拉丁欧洲。教皇尤金三世颁布诏书，克莱尔沃的伯尔纳鼓动第二次十字军东征；1148年十字军在大马士革城下失败，反而增强了赞吉之子努尔丁的力量。

name.en: Rustaveli’s The Knight in the Panther’s Skin

summary.en: Shota Rustaveli, a courtier of Queen Tamar, composed this epic of friendship, love and chivalry set in Arabia and India. It is Georgia’s national poem; until the 20th century a copy was traditionally part of a bride’s dowry.
summary.zh: 塔玛尔女王的廷臣绍塔·鲁斯塔韦利创作了这部以阿拉伯和印度为背景、歌颂友谊、爱情与骑士精神的史诗。它是格鲁吉亚的民族诗篇；直到20世纪，按传统新娘的嫁妆里都要有一部抄本。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: The Knight in the Panther's Skin
D. Rayfield, The Literature of Georgia: A History (3rd ed., 2010)
Wikipedia: The Knight in the Panther%27s Skin

note: Composed in the late 12th or early 13th century; nothing certain is known of Rustaveli’s life.

name.zh: 阿卡之围（第三次十字军东征）

summary.en: Guy of Lusignan began besieging Acre in 1189 and was himself besieged by Saladin’s army. After two years of attrition, the arrival of Philip II of France and Richard I of England forced the garrison to surrender in July 1191; Acre became the new crusader capital.
summary.zh: 1189年吕西尼昂的居伊开始围攻阿卡，自己又被萨拉丁的军队包围。经过两年消耗战，法王腓力二世和英王理查一世到来，迫使守军于1191年7月投降；阿卡成为十字军的新首都。

sources.title: Bahaʾ al-Din Ibn Shaddad, The Rare and Excellent History of Saladin (trans. D. S. Richards, 2001)

story.en:
After Hattin, Saladin took almost every crusader town, but Tyre held out, and King Guy of Lusignan, released from captivity, marched on Acre in August 1189 with only a few thousand men. Saladin's army soon arrived and surrounded the besiegers, so that for two years a crusader camp was itself trapped between the city walls and the sultan's lines.

Ships from Pisa, Denmark, Flanders and England kept arriving, and disease, famine and winter killed thousands on both sides, including Queen Sibylla. Saladin's secretary Baha' al-Din describes swimmers carrying messages and gold into the city, and Greek fire burning the crusaders' siege towers.

Philip II arrived in April 1191 and Richard I in June; their heavy siege engines broke the walls and the garrison surrendered on 12 July. When ransom talks stalled, Richard had some 2,700 Muslim prisoners killed in August. The Third Crusade went on to win at Arsuf but never retook Jerusalem; the 1192 Treaty of Jaffa left a coastal kingdom ruled from Acre for another century.
story.zh:
哈丁之战后，萨拉丁几乎攻下了所有十字军城镇，只有提尔坚守不降。获释的居伊国王于1189年8月仅率数千人进军阿卡。萨拉丁大军随即赶到，反把围城者包围，于是两年间十字军营地被夹在城墙与苏丹的阵线之间。

来自比萨、丹麦、佛兰德和英格兰的船只陆续抵达，疾病、饥荒和寒冬使双方数以千计的人丧生，西比拉王后也死于营中。萨拉丁的秘书巴哈丁记述了泅水者把信件和黄金送进城中，以及希腊火烧毁十字军攻城塔的情景。

腓力二世于1191年4月到达，理查一世6月到达，他们的重型攻城器械击破城墙，守军于7月12日投降。赎金谈判陷入僵局后，理查于8月下令处死约2700名穆斯林俘虏。第三次十字军随后在阿尔苏夫获胜，却始终未能夺回耶路撒冷；1192年《雅法条约》留下了一个以阿卡为都的沿海王国，又延续了一个世纪。

summary.en: A Mongol army under Baiju routed Sultan Kaykhusraw II of Rum in the mountains north-east of Sivas, on the road to Erzincan. The Seljuk sultanate became a Mongol vassal paying heavy tribute, and its slow collapse opened Anatolia to the frontier beyliks from which the Ottomans emerged.
summary.zh: 拜住率领的蒙古军在锡瓦斯东北、通往埃尔津詹途中的山区击溃罗姆苏丹凯霍斯鲁二世。塞尔柱苏丹国沦为蒙古附庸并缴纳重贡，其缓慢瓦解使安纳托利亚出现了众多边境侯国，奥斯曼人便由此崛起。

sources.title: C. Cahen, The Formation of Turkey (2001)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Köse Dağ

story.en:
In the 1230s the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum was at its height: Konya, Kayseri and Sivas were full of new mosques and caravanserais, and Kaykubad I had added Alanya and a foothold in the Crimea to its earlier ports on the Black Sea and the Mediterranean. His son Kaykhusraw II inherited a rich state but faced a Turkmen revolt and, to the east, the Mongol armies that had conquered Iran and Georgia.

In the winter of 1242–43 the Mongol commander Baiju took Erzurum. Kaykhusraw gathered a large army including Georgian, Armenian and Frankish mercenaries and met him at Köse Dağ on 26 June. The Mongols seem to have used a feigned retreat to draw the Seljuk vanguard into a trap; the sultan's army broke and fled, and Kaykhusraw abandoned his camp and treasure.

The battle was quick but decisive. Rum survived only as a Mongol tributary, later under Ilkhanid governors. As central authority withered, Turkmen chiefs in the west built their own principalities, among them the small beylik of Osman.
story.zh:
1230年代，罗姆塞尔柱苏丹国处于鼎盛：科尼亚、开塞利和锡瓦斯新建了大量清真寺和商队客栈，凯库巴德一世在原有的黑海与地中海港口之外，又夺得阿兰亚并在克里米亚立足。其子凯霍斯鲁二世继承了一个富庶的国家，却面临土库曼人叛乱，东方又有已征服伊朗和格鲁吉亚的蒙古大军。

1242至1243年冬，蒙古统帅拜住攻占埃尔祖鲁姆。凯霍斯鲁集结了包括格鲁吉亚、亚美尼亚和法兰克雇佣兵在内的大军，6月26日在克塞山迎战。蒙古人似乎以佯退诱使塞尔柱先锋陷入埋伏；苏丹军队溃散，凯霍斯鲁丢下营帐和财宝逃走。

这场战斗短促却具有决定性。罗姆此后只能作为蒙古的纳贡国苟存，后来又受伊利汗国总督管辖。随着中央权威衰落，西部的土库曼首领纷纷建立自己的侯国，其中就有奥斯曼的小侯国。

summary.en: The Mamluk sultan al-Ashraf Khalil besieged Acre with a huge army and siege engines; after six weeks the walls were breached on 18 May. The last crusader cities of the coast, Tyre, Sidon, Beirut and Tortosa, were abandoned within months, ending two centuries of crusader states on the Levantine mainland (the Templars kept the islet of Ruad until 1302).
summary.zh: 马穆鲁克苏丹阿什拉夫·哈利勒率大军和攻城器械围攻阿卡，六周后于5月18日攻破城墙。沿海最后的十字军城市提尔、西顿、贝鲁特和托尔托萨在数月内相继被放弃，黎凡特大陆上的十字军国家两百年历史至此结束（圣殿骑士团守住鲁阿德小岛直至1302年）。

sources.title: Abu al-Fida, Memoirs (eyewitness of the siege)

story.en:
By 1291 the Kingdom of Jerusalem was a strip of coastal towns, with Acre as its crowded capital of merchants, military orders and rival Italian quarters. Baybars and his successor Qalawun had already taken Antioch, Krak des Chevaliers and Tripoli. When Italian crusaders killed Muslim merchants in Acre in 1290, Qalawun prepared a final campaign; he died before it began, and his son al-Ashraf Khalil led it.

The Mamluk army arrived in early April 1291 with dozens of siege engines; the young prince Abu al-Fida, later a historian, helped haul one of them. Sappers undermined the towers, and on 18 May the attackers stormed through the Accursed Tower. Defenders and civilians crowded the harbour; the Templars held their seafront fortress for ten more days before it collapsed.

Khalil had the walls razed so the Franks could not return. Within weeks the remaining crusader towns surrendered or were evacuated, and the military orders withdrew to Cyprus. Acre recovered only slowly, under the Ottomans.
story.zh:
到1291年，耶路撒冷王国只剩一串沿海城镇，阿卡是其拥挤的首都，聚集着商人、骑士团和相互竞争的意大利街区。拜巴尔及其继任者盖拉温已经攻下安条克、骑士堡和的黎波里。1290年意大利十字军在阿卡杀害穆斯林商人，盖拉温遂筹备最后一战；他在出征前去世，由其子阿什拉夫·哈利勒统军。

1291年4月初，马穆鲁克大军携数十台攻城器械抵达；年轻的王子阿布·菲达（后来成为历史学家）也参与拖运其中一台。工兵挖空了塔楼地基，5月18日进攻者从“诅咒之塔”攻入城中。守军和平民挤满港口；圣殿骑士团在海边堡垒中又坚守了十天，直到堡垒坍塌。

哈利勒下令拆毁城墙，使法兰克人无法卷土重来。数周之内其余十字军城镇或投降或撤离，各骑士团退往塞浦路斯。阿卡直到奥斯曼时期才逐渐恢复。

summary.en: Commissioned by Ghazan and finished under Öljeitü, Rashid al-Din’s Jami' al-tawarikh combined Mongol oral tradition with histories of China, India, the Franks and the Jews. Illustrated copies made in his Tabriz workshop are masterpieces of Persian painting.
summary.zh: 拉施德丁的《史集》由合赞下令编撰，在完者都时完成，融合了蒙古口传历史以及中国、印度、法兰克人和犹太人的历史。他在大不里士作坊中绘制的插图本是波斯绘画的杰作。

sources.title: S. S. Blair, A Compendium of Chronicles: Rashid al-Din's Illustrated History of the World (1995)

note: The first version was presented in 1307 (706 AH); work continued until c. 1310.

summary.en: After a blockade of several years, the Byzantine city of Prusa surrendered to Orhan, son of Osman. As Bursa it became the first Ottoman capital and the burial place of the dynasty’s founders.
summary.zh: 经过数年封锁，拜占庭城市普鲁萨向奥斯曼之子奥尔汗投降。改称布尔萨后，它成为奥斯曼的第一个首都和王朝创建者的安葬地。

sources.title: H. İnalcık, "Osman Ghazi's Siege of Nicaea and the Battle of Bapheus", in The Ottoman Emirate (1993)

summary.en: Mehmed II’s artillery and janissaries defeated Uzun Hasan of the Aq Qoyunlu near Erzincan, ending his hopes, encouraged by Venice, of a grand alliance against the Ottomans and securing eastern Anatolia for the empire.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德二世的火炮和近卫军在埃尔津詹附近击败白羊王朝的乌宗·哈桑，粉碎了他在威尼斯鼓动下组建反奥斯曼大同盟的希望，使安纳托利亚东部归于奥斯曼帝国。

sources.title: J. E. Woods, The Aqquyunlu (rev. ed., 1999)

summary.en: Discharged musketeers, unpaid troops and impoverished peasants formed rebel armies that ravaged Anatolia during the long war with the Habsburgs. Kuyucu Murad Pasha suppressed them brutally by 1610, but the "Great Flight" from the countryside left villages deserted for generations.
summary.zh: 在与哈布斯堡王朝的长期战争中，被遣散的火枪手、欠饷士兵和贫困农民组成叛军，蹂躏安纳托利亚。到1610年库尤朱·穆拉德帕夏以残酷手段将其镇压，但“大逃亡”使乡村荒废了好几代人。

sources.title: W. J. Griswold, The Great Anatolian Rebellion, 1000–1020/1591–1611 (1983)
S. White, The Climate of Rebellion in the Early Modern Ottoman Empire (2011)

note: "Celali" revolts recur from 1519 to the 1650s; this record marks the great wave of c. 1595–1610, centred on central Anatolia (plotted at Kayseri).

name.zh: 英波联军攻占霍尔木兹

summary.en: Shah Abbas I’s army, carried and supported by ships of the English East India Company, took the Portuguese fortress on Hormuz island after a ten-week siege. Gulf trade shifted to the mainland port of Gombroon, renamed Bandar Abbas.
summary.zh: 阿拔斯一世的军队在英国东印度公司船只的运送和支援下，经十周围攻攻下霍尔木兹岛上的葡萄牙要塞。海湾贸易随之转移到大陆上的港口贡布隆，该港随即更名为阿巴斯港。

sources.title: R. Matthee, The Politics of Trade in Safavid Iran (1999)

name.zh: 穆拉德四世收复巴格达

summary.en: Sultan Murad IV personally led the siege that recovered Baghdad from the Safavids, who had held it since 1624. The Treaty of Zuhab the next year left Iraq Ottoman and fixed a frontier that roughly survives as the Iran–Iraq border.
summary.zh: 苏丹穆拉德四世亲自率军围攻，从1624年起占据巴格达的萨法维人手中收复该城。次年的《祖哈布条约》使伊拉克归属奥斯曼，确定的边界大致延续为今天的伊朗-伊拉克边界。

sources.title: C. Finkel, Osman's Dream: The History of the Ottoman Empire (2005)

name.zh: 沙巴泰·泽维弥赛亚运动

summary.en: In 1665 the Smyrna-born rabbi Sabbatai Zevi was proclaimed the Messiah, and enthusiasm swept Jewish communities from Yemen to Amsterdam. Arrested by the Ottomans, he converted to Islam before the sultan at Edirne in September 1666; a small Dönme community followed him.
summary.zh: 1665年，出生于士麦那的拉比沙巴泰·泽维被宣布为弥赛亚，从也门到阿姆斯特丹的犹太社区掀起狂热。他被奥斯曼当局逮捕，1666年9月在埃迪尔内当着苏丹的面皈依伊斯兰教；一小批追随者形成了“东马”社团。

sources.title: G. Scholem, Sabbatai Ṣevi: The Mystical Messiah (1973)

name.zh: 阿富汗人围攻伊斯法罕

summary.en: Mahmud Hotak’s Ghilzai Afghans defeated the Safavid army at Gulnabad and starved Isfahan through a seven-month siege in which tens of thousands died. Shah Sultan Husayn abdicated in October, and Safavid rule effectively ended.
summary.zh: 马哈茂德·霍塔克率领的吉尔扎伊阿富汗人在古尔纳巴德击败萨法维军，又围困伊斯法罕七个月，城中数万人饿死。10月苏丹·侯赛因沙退位，萨法维统治实际告终。

sources.title: R. Matthee, Persia in Crisis: Safavid Decline and the Fall of Isfahan (2012)
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Isfahan x. Safavid period

name.zh: 格奥尔吉耶夫斯克条约

summary.en: Heraclius II of Kartli-Kakheti placed his kingdom under Russian protection, renouncing Persian suzerainty. Russia withdrew its troops in 1787 and did not help when Persia attacked in 1795, but used the treaty to justify annexation in 1801.
summary.zh: 卡特利-卡赫季国王赫拉克利乌斯二世宣布放弃波斯宗主权，将王国置于俄国保护之下。俄国于1787年撤军，1795年波斯进攻时也未援救，却在1801年以该条约为吞并的依据。

sources.title: R. G. Suny, The Making of the Georgian Nation (2nd ed., 1994)

name.en: Battle of Krtsanisi and sack of Tbilisi
name.zh: 克尔察尼西战役与第比利斯之劫

summary.en: Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar, determined to restore Persian rule in the Caucasus, crushed the outnumbered army of the elderly Heraclius II outside Tbilisi and sacked the city, carrying off thousands of captives. Russia responded by annexing eastern Georgia in 1801.
summary.zh: 决意恢复波斯对高加索统治的阿迦·穆罕默德汗·恺加在第比利斯城外击溃年迈的赫拉克利乌斯二世寡不敌众的军队，洗劫全城，掳走数千人。俄国随后于1801年吞并东格鲁吉亚。

sources.title: D. Rayfield, Edge of Empires: A History of Georgia (2012)
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Āḡā Moḥammad Khan Qājār

summary.en: At the sultan’s request, Muhammad Ali of Egypt sent armies under his sons Tusun and Ibrahim to recover the holy cities from the first Saudi state. Ibrahim Pasha besieged and razed Diriyah in 1818; the emir Abdullah ibn Saud was executed in Istanbul.
summary.zh: 应苏丹要求，埃及的穆罕默德·阿里派儿子图松和易卜拉欣率军从第一沙特国手中收复圣城。1818年易卜拉欣帕夏围攻并夷平德拉伊耶；埃米尔阿卜杜拉·本·沙特在伊斯坦布尔被处决。

label.zh: 易卜拉欣经盖西姆推进

sources.title: M. Al-Rasheed, A History of Saudi Arabia (2nd ed., 2010)
K. Fahmy, All the Pasha's Men (1997)

summary.en: Ending the Russo-Persian war of 1804–13, Qajar Iran recognised Russian rule over Georgia, Dagestan and most of today’s Azerbaijan, including Baku, Ganja and Karabakh, and gave up navy rights on the Caspian.
summary.zh: 该条约结束了1804–1813年的俄波战争，恺加伊朗承认俄国对格鲁吉亚、达吉斯坦以及今阿塞拜疆大部（包括巴库、占贾和卡拉巴赫）的统治，并放弃在里海保有海军的权利。

note: Signed at the village of Gulistan in Karabakh; the coordinate is approximate.

name.en: Edict of Gülhane opens the Tanzimat
name.zh: 花厅御诏开启坦志麦特改革

summary.en: Read out in the Gülhane rose garden of Topkapı Palace, the Hatt-ı Şerif promised all Ottoman subjects, Muslim and non-Muslim, security of life and property, fair taxation and regular conscription. It began four decades of Tanzimat ("reorganisation") reforms.
summary.zh: 《花厅御诏》在托普卡帕宫的花厅玫瑰园宣读，承诺保障所有奥斯曼臣民（无论穆斯林与否）的生命财产安全、公平征税和规范征兵，由此开启长达四十年的坦志麦特（“整顿”）改革。

sources.title: C. V. Findley, Turkey, Islam, Nationalism, and Modernity (2010)

summary.en: In Shiraz the merchant Sayyid Ali Muhammad declared himself the Báb ("Gate"), founding the Bábí movement. The Qajar state and clergy suppressed it bloodily and executed him at Tabriz in 1850; most Bábís later followed Bahá'u'lláh into the Bahá'í Faith.
summary.zh: 商人赛义德·阿里·穆罕默德在设拉子自称“巴孛”（意为“门”），创立巴比教。恺加政府和教士对其血腥镇压，1850年在大不里士将他处决；后来大多数巴比教徒追随巴哈欧拉，形成巴哈伊教。

sources.title: A. Amanat, Resurrection and Renewal: The Making of the Babi Movement in Iran (1989)

name.en: 1860 civil war in Mount Lebanon and Damascus
name.zh: 1860年黎巴嫩山与大马士革内乱

summary.en: Conflict between Druze and Maronite Christians in Mount Lebanon spread to Damascus, where thousands of Christians were killed in July. France landed troops, and an international commission created an autonomous Mount Lebanon governed by a Christian mutasarrif (1861–1915, formally until 1918).
summary.zh: 黎巴嫩山区德鲁兹派与马龙派基督徒的冲突蔓延到大马士革，7月有数千名基督徒遇害。法国派兵登陆，国际委员会随后设立由基督徒总督治理的黎巴嫩山自治区（1861–1915，名义上延续至1918年）。

sources.title: L. T. Fawaz, An Occasion for War: Civil Conflict in Lebanon and Damascus in 1860 (1994)
Wikipedia: 1860 civil conflict in Mount Lebanon and Damascus

note: Plotted at Deir al-Qamar, scene of one of the worst massacres in June 1860.

summary.en: Naser al-Din Shah granted a British subject a monopoly over Iran’s tobacco trade. Merchants and clerics mobilised, and a fatwa attributed to Mirza Hasan Shirazi forbidding tobacco led to a nationwide boycott; the shah cancelled the concession in January 1892.
summary.zh: 纳赛尔丁沙把伊朗烟草贸易专营权授予一名英国人。商人和宗教人士发动抗议，一份署名米尔扎·哈桑·设拉齐的禁烟教令引发全国抵制；1892年1月国王被迫取消特许权。

sources.title: N. R. Keddie, Religion and Rebellion in Iran: The Tobacco Protest of 1891–1892 (1966)

summary.en: After Armenians in Sasun resisted double taxation, Ottoman troops and Kurdish Hamidiye irregulars began a wave of massacres across the eastern provinces and in Istanbul under Sultan Abdulhamid II. Estimates of the dead range from about 100,000 to 300,000.
summary.zh: 萨松的亚美尼亚人抵制双重征税后，在苏丹阿卜杜勒哈米德二世统治下，奥斯曼军队和库尔德“哈米德”非正规骑兵在东部各省及伊斯坦布尔发动一波屠杀。死亡人数估计约为10万至30万。

sources.title: R. G. Suny, "They Can Live in the Desert but Nowhere Else": A History of the Armenian Genocide (2015)

note: Death toll estimates vary widely; plotted at Sasun, where the violence began in 1894.

summary.en: General Townshend’s Anglo-Indian division, retreating after a failed advance on Baghdad, was besieged at Kut al-Amara for 147 days. Relief attempts cost some 23,000 casualties; about 13,000 men surrendered in April 1916, and many died on the march into captivity.
summary.zh: 汤森将军的英印师进攻巴格达失败后撤退，被围困在库特阿马拉达147天。解围行动伤亡约2.3万人；1916年4月约1.3万人投降，许多人死于前往战俘营的行军途中。

sources.title: C. Townshend, When God Made Hell: The British Invasion of Mesopotamia (2010)

summary.en: After breaking the Gaza–Beersheba line, Allenby’s Egyptian Expeditionary Force took Jerusalem; the mayor surrendered on 9 December and Allenby entered on foot through the Jaffa Gate two days later. A month earlier Britain’s Balfour Declaration had backed a Jewish "national home" in Palestine.
summary.zh: 艾伦比的埃及远征军突破加沙—贝尔谢巴防线后攻占耶路撒冷；12月9日市长出城投降，两天后艾伦比步行经雅法门入城。一个月前，英国发表《贝尔福宣言》，支持在巴勒斯坦建立犹太“民族家园”。

sources.title: E. Rogan, The Fall of the Ottomans (2015)

summary.en: After the Ottoman defeat, Mustafa Kemal organised a nationalist movement in Anatolia that fought Armenian, French and above all Greek armies and defied the Treaty of Sèvres. Victory in 1922 led to the Treaty of Lausanne (1923), which recognised a Turkish state in Anatolia and eastern Thrace.
summary.zh: 奥斯曼战败后，穆斯塔法·凯末尔在安纳托利亚组织民族主义运动，与亚美尼亚、法国，尤其是希腊军队作战，拒不接受《色佛尔条约》。1922年的胜利促成1923年《洛桑条约》，承认在安纳托利亚和东色雷斯建立土耳其国家。

label.zh: 凯末尔在萨姆松登陆（5月19日）

label.en: Grand National Assembly opens in Ankara
label.zh: 大国民议会在安卡拉开幕
收复士麦那（伊兹密尔），城市遭焚

sources.title: E. J. Zürcher, Turkey: A Modern History (3rd ed., 2004)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Turkish War of Independence

story.en:
The armistice of Mudros in October 1918 left the Ottoman Empire occupied: Allied ships lay off Istanbul, French troops held Cilicia, and in May 1919 a Greek army landed at Smyrna with Allied approval. A few days later Mustafa Kemal, hero of Gallipoli, landed at Samsun on the Black Sea, officially as an army inspector. He resigned his commission and, at congresses in Erzurum and Sivas, organised resistance around a "National Pact" for an undivided Turkish homeland.

In April 1920 a Grand National Assembly met in the small town of Ankara and rejected the Treaty of Sèvres that the Sultan's government signed in August. Nationalist forces fought the Armenian republic in the east, pushed the French out of Cilicia and, in 1921, halted the Greek advance on Ankara after a 22-day battle on the Sakarya River.

The Great Offensive of August 1922 broke the Greek front; Turkish cavalry entered Smyrna on 9 September, and a great fire destroyed its Greek and Armenian quarters. The Treaty of Lausanne in July 1923 recognised the new Turkey and provided for a compulsory exchange of Orthodox Christian and Muslim populations between Greece and Turkey.
story.zh:
1918年10月的穆德洛斯停战协定使奥斯曼帝国处于占领之下：协约国舰队停泊在伊斯坦布尔外海，法军占据奇里乞亚，1919年5月希腊军队经协约国同意在士麦那登陆。几天后，加里波利英雄穆斯塔法·凯末尔以陆军督察身份在黑海边的萨姆松登陆。他随即辞去军职，在埃尔祖鲁姆和锡瓦斯大会上围绕主张土耳其本土不可分割的《国民公约》组织抵抗。

1920年4月，大国民议会在小城安卡拉召开，拒绝承认苏丹政府8月签署的《色佛尔条约》。民族主义军队在东方与亚美尼亚共和国作战，把法军逐出奇里乞亚，并于1921年在萨卡里亚河畔经过22天激战阻止了希腊军对安卡拉的进攻。

1922年8月的大反攻击溃希腊战线；9月9日土耳其骑兵进入士麦那，一场大火烧毁了城中的希腊人和亚美尼亚人街区。1923年7月的《洛桑条约》承认新土耳其，并规定希腊与土耳其之间强制交换东正教徒和穆斯林人口。

summary.en: Shi'i and Sunni tribes, clerics and nationalists rose against British rule after the mandate was announced. The revolt, beginning at Rumaytha in June, was put down by October with heavy losses on both sides, and Britain chose to govern through an Arab monarchy under Faisal.
summary.zh: 委任统治宣布后，什叶派和逊尼派部落、宗教人士及民族主义者起而反抗英国统治。起义6月从鲁迈塞开始，到10月被镇压，双方伤亡惨重；英国此后决定通过费萨尔领导的阿拉伯君主政体来统治。

sources.title: C. Tripp, A History of Iraq (3rd ed., 2007)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Iraq: The British mandate

summary.en: A law passed on 1 November 1928 replaced the Arabic script with a new Latin-based alphabet for Turkish. Atatürk toured the country with a chalkboard to teach it, and the change cut the new republic’s readers off from Ottoman-era writing.
summary.zh: 1928年11月1日通过的法律以新的拉丁字母取代阿拉伯字母书写土耳其语。阿塔图尔克带着黑板巡回全国教授新字母，这一改变也使新共和国的读者与奥斯曼时代的文献产生了隔阂。

sources.title: G. Lewis, The Turkish Language Reform: A Catastrophic Success (1999)

name.en: Oil found in commercial quantities at Dammam No. 7
name.zh: 达曼7号井发现商业石油

summary.en: After six dry or disappointing wells, the American company Casoc struck oil at Dammam No. 7 near Dhahran in March 1938. It began Saudi Arabia’s transformation into the world’s leading oil exporter and the later Aramco partnership.
summary.zh: 在六口井无果或不尽如人意之后，美国公司卡索克于1938年3月在宰赫兰附近的达曼7号井打出石油。沙特阿拉伯由此开始转变为世界头号石油出口国，也开启了后来的阿美石油公司合作。

story.en:
In 1933 Ibn Saud, short of money as the Depression cut pilgrim revenues, granted an oil concession over eastern Arabia to Standard Oil of California for a down payment in gold. Its subsidiary, the California Arabian Standard Oil Company (Casoc), began drilling on the Dammam dome near Dhahran in 1935, encouraged by the oil found on nearby Bahrain three years earlier.

The first wells disappointed, and in San Francisco executives questioned whether to continue. The geologist Max Steineke argued for drilling deeper, and Dammam No. 7, begun in December 1936, went down past the earlier depths. In early March 1938, at about 1,440 metres, it began flowing more than 1,500 barrels a day. It went on producing for decades and was renamed Prosperity Well.

In May 1939 Ibn Saud travelled to Ras Tanura to open the valve for the first tanker. The discovery turned the kingdom into an oil state; Casoc became Aramco, and after the Second World War Saudi revenues and the US-Saudi relationship grew together.
story.zh:
1933年，大萧条使朝觐收入锐减，手头拮据的伊本·沙特以收取一笔黄金预付款为条件，把东阿拉伯的石油特许权授予加利福尼亚标准石油公司。受三年前邻近的巴林发现石油的鼓舞，其子公司加利福尼亚阿拉伯标准石油公司（卡索克）于1935年开始在宰赫兰附近的达曼穹隆钻探。

最初几口井令人失望，旧金山的高管们一度怀疑是否该继续。地质学家马克斯·斯坦内克主张钻得更深，1936年12月开钻的达曼7号井越过了以往的深度。1938年3月初，钻至约1440米时开始日产1500多桶。这口井此后持续出油数十年，被命名为“繁荣井”。

1939年5月，伊本·沙特亲赴拉斯坦努拉，为第一艘油轮开启阀门。这一发现把王国变成石油国家；卡索克改组为阿美石油公司，二战后沙特的石油收入与美沙关系同步增长。

summary.en: Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill met for the first time, in Tehran, which Allied forces had occupied since 1941. They agreed on an Anglo-American invasion of France in 1944 and, in a declaration, promised Iran its independence after the war.
summary.zh: 斯大林、罗斯福和丘吉尔首次会晤，地点在1941年起被盟军占领的德黑兰。他们商定1944年英美进攻法国，并在一份宣言中承诺战后维护伊朗独立。

sources.title: Foreign Relations of the United States: The Conferences at Cairo and Tehran, 1943 (1961)

summary.en: Civil war in Mandatory Palestine became an interstate war when Egypt, Transjordan, Syria, Iraq and Lebanon intervened after Israel’s declaration in May 1948. Israel survived and enlarged its territory; over 700,000 Palestinian Arabs fled or were expelled, the Nakba ("catastrophe"). The 1949 armistice lines became the "Green Line".
summary.zh: 1948年5月以色列宣布建国后，埃及、外约旦、叙利亚、伊拉克和黎巴嫩出兵，巴勒斯坦托管地的内战演变为国家间战争。以色列存续下来并扩大了领土；七十多万巴勒斯坦阿拉伯人逃离或被驱逐，即“纳克巴”（“浩劫”）。1949年的停战线成为“绿线”。

sources.title: B. Morris, 1948: A History of the First Arab–Israeli War (2008)
E. L. Rogan and A. Shlaim (eds.), The War for Palestine (2nd ed., 2007)

note: Plotted at Latrun, on the contested road to Jerusalem.

story.en:
When the United Nations voted in November 1947 to partition Palestine into Jewish and Arab states, the Jewish leadership accepted and Arab leaders rejected the plan, and fighting broke out between the two communities. In April 1948 the Haganah went on the offensive to secure the areas allotted to the Jewish state and the road to besieged West Jerusalem; the killing of villagers at Deir Yassin that month spread fear across Arab Palestine.

On 14 May, as the British left, David Ben-Gurion proclaimed the State of Israel, and the next day armies from Egypt, Transjordan, Syria, Iraq and Lebanon crossed the borders. Transjordan's Arab Legion held the Old City of Jerusalem and the hills around Latrun, but in a series of campaigns Israeli forces took Galilee, the coastal plain and much of the Negev, ending with more territory than the UN plan had given.

By the 1949 armistices more than 700,000 Palestinian Arabs had fled or been driven from their homes, and Israel did not allow them to return. Palestinians mark the Nakba on 15 May. The causes of the exodus, flight from war or deliberate expulsion, as at Lydda and Ramle in July 1948, remain argued over by historians, and the refugee question is still unresolved.
story.zh:
1947年11月联合国表决把巴勒斯坦分为犹太国和阿拉伯国，犹太领导层接受而阿拉伯领导人拒绝，两个社群之间爆发战斗。1948年4月哈加纳转入进攻，以控制分给犹太国的地区和通往被围西耶路撒冷的道路；同月代尔亚辛村民遭杀害，恐慌在阿拉伯巴勒斯坦蔓延。

5月14日英国撤离之际，戴维·本-古里安宣布以色列建国，次日埃及、外约旦、叙利亚、伊拉克和黎巴嫩军队越过边界。外约旦的阿拉伯军团守住了耶路撒冷老城和拉特伦周围的山地，但以色列军队通过一系列战役夺取了加利利、沿海平原和内盖夫大部，最终控制的领土超过联合国分治方案的划分。

到1949年停战时，七十多万巴勒斯坦阿拉伯人逃离或被逐出家园，以色列不允许他们返回。巴勒斯坦人在5月15日纪念“纳克巴”。这场出走的原因，是躲避战火还是有意驱逐（如1948年7月的吕大和拉姆勒），历史学家至今争论不休，难民问题也仍未解决。

name.zh: 伊拉克七月十四日革命

summary.en: Officers led by Abd al-Karim Qasim and Abd al-Salam Arif overthrew the Hashemite monarchy; King Faisal II and much of the royal family were killed at the palace, and prime minister Nuri al-Said was killed the next day. Iraq became a republic and in 1959 left the pro-Western Baghdad Pact.
summary.zh: 阿卜杜勒-卡里姆·卡塞姆和阿卜杜勒-萨拉姆·阿里夫领导的军官推翻哈希姆君主制；国王费萨尔二世和大部分王室成员在王宫遇害，首相努里·赛义德次日被杀。伊拉克成为共和国，并于1959年退出亲西方的巴格达条约组织。

sources.title: H. Batatu, The Old Social Classes and the Revolutionary Movements of Iraq (1978)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Iraq: The revolution of 1958

summary.en: Amid rising tension and Egypt’s closure of the Straits of Tiran, Israel launched surprise air strikes on 5 June 1967 and in six days took Sinai and Gaza from Egypt, the West Bank and East Jerusalem from Jordan, and the Golan Heights from Syria. UN Resolution 242 set the "land for peace" formula.
summary.zh: 在局势日益紧张、埃及封锁蒂朗海峡之际，以色列于1967年6月5日发动突然空袭，六天内从埃及手中夺取西奈半岛和加沙，从约旦手中夺取约旦河西岸和东耶路撒冷，从叙利亚手中夺取戈兰高地。联合国第242号决议确立了“以土地换和平”的原则。

sources.title: M. B. Oren, Six Days of War (2002)

story.en:
In May 1967 Egypt's president Nasser, responding to Soviet reports of Israeli troop build-ups against Syria, moved forces into Sinai, had UN peacekeepers withdrawn and closed the Straits of Tiran to Israeli shipping. Jordan signed a defence pact with Egypt. In Israel, fear of encirclement grew during weeks of waiting.

On the morning of 5 June the Israeli air force struck Egyptian airfields and destroyed most of Egypt's air force on the ground within hours. Ground forces then broke through in Sinai and reached the Suez Canal. When Jordan opened fire, Israeli troops took East Jerusalem and the West Bank; paratroopers reached the Western Wall on 7 June. On the last two days Israel stormed the Golan Heights.

The war tripled the territory under Israeli control and brought about a million Palestinians under military occupation, while some 250,000 more fled, many for the second time. The Arab defeat discredited Nasserism, and UN Resolution 242 called for withdrawal from territories occupied in exchange for peace, a formula still at the centre of diplomacy.
story.zh:
1967年5月，埃及总统纳赛尔因苏联通报以色列正在对叙利亚集结兵力，向西奈派兵，要求联合国维和部队撤离，并对以色列船只封锁蒂朗海峡。约旦与埃及签订防务协定。以色列国内在数周的等待中担心被包围的情绪日益高涨。

6月5日清晨，以色列空军突袭埃及机场，几小时内摧毁了埃及空军大部分停放在地面的飞机。地面部队随即突破西奈防线，直抵苏伊士运河。约旦开火后，以军攻占东耶路撒冷和约旦河西岸，伞兵于6月7日抵达西墙。最后两天，以色列强攻戈兰高地。

战争使以色列控制的领土增加了两倍，约一百万巴勒斯坦人处于军事占领之下，另有约二十五万人逃离，许多人是第二次沦为难民。阿拉伯的失败使纳赛尔主义声誉扫地；联合国第242号决议要求以撤出占领领土换取和平，这一原则至今仍是外交的核心。

name.zh: 阿拉伯联合酋长国成立

summary.en: As Britain ended its treaty protection of the Trucial States, six emirates led by Sheikh Zayed of Abu Dhabi and Sheikh Rashid of Dubai formed a federation; Ras al-Khaimah joined in February 1972. Oil wealth turned the coast of fishing and pearling towns into global hubs.
summary.zh: 英国结束对“特鲁西尔诸国”的条约保护之际，阿布扎比的扎耶德谢赫和迪拜的拉希德谢赫领导六个酋长国组成联邦；哈伊马角于1972年2月加入。石油财富把这片以捕鱼和采珠为生的海岸变成了全球枢纽。

sources.title: F. Heard-Bey, From Trucial States to United Arab Emirates (2004)

note: Plotted at Union House in Dubai, where the union was signed.

name.en: Yom Kippur (October) War and oil embargo
name.zh: 赎罪日战争（十月战争）与石油禁运

summary.en: Egypt and Syria attacked on the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, crossing the Suez Canal and storming the Golan. Israel recovered and counter-attacked before a ceasefire on 25 October. Arab oil producers’ embargo quadrupled oil prices, and the war opened the way to the Egypt–Israel peace of 1979.
summary.zh: 埃及和叙利亚在犹太教赎罪日发动进攻，越过苏伊士运河并猛攻戈兰高地。以色列稳住阵脚并反击，10月25日停火。阿拉伯产油国的禁运使油价上涨四倍，这场战争也为1979年埃以和约铺平了道路。

sources.title: A. Rabinovich, The Yom Kippur War (2004)

note: Plotted on the Golan front; the Sinai front lies in Africa.

story.en:
After 1967 Egypt's new president Anwar Sadat concluded that only a war, however limited, would force diplomacy over Sinai. Egypt and Syria planned in secret, and Israeli intelligence, confident in its "concept" that Egypt would not attack without air superiority, dismissed the warnings until the last hours.

At 2 p.m. on 6 October 1973, Yom Kippur, Egyptian troops crossed the Suez Canal in boats, used high-pressure water cannon to cut through the sand ramparts of the Bar-Lev line, and set up a missile umbrella that cost Israel heavily in aircraft and tanks. On the Golan, Syrian armour nearly broke through to the Sea of Galilee before reserves held it. In the third week Israeli forces crossed the canal and encircled Egypt's Third Army, and the superpowers imposed a ceasefire.

Arab members of OPEC cut output and embargoed the United States and the Netherlands; oil prices roughly quadrupled within months, a shock felt worldwide. The partial success restored Egyptian pride, led to disengagement talks and, via Camp David, to the 1979 peace treaty, while in Israel the Agranat Commission's findings helped end Golda Meir's government.
story.zh:
1967年后，埃及新总统萨达特认定，只有发动一场哪怕是有限的战争，才能迫使各方就西奈问题展开外交。埃及和叙利亚秘密筹划，以色列情报部门坚信埃及在没有空中优势时不会进攻的“概念”，直到最后几小时仍对警告不以为然。

1973年10月6日赎罪日下午2时，埃及军队乘船渡过苏伊士运河，用高压水炮冲开巴列夫防线的沙墙，并构建导弹防空伞，使以色列损失大量飞机和坦克。在戈兰高地，叙利亚装甲部队几乎突破到加利利海，直到以军预备队赶到才被挡住。第三周以军渡过运河，包围埃及第三军团，两个超级大国随后促成停火。

欧佩克中的阿拉伯成员国减产，并对美国和荷兰实施禁运；数月内油价上涨约四倍，冲击波及全球。部分胜利恢复了埃及的自尊，促成了脱离接触谈判，并经戴维营会谈达成1979年和约；在以色列，阿格拉纳特委员会的调查结论促使果尔达·梅厄政府下台。

summary.en: Tensions between Christian militias, Palestinian guerrillas and Muslim and leftist parties exploded in 1975 and drew in Syria, Israel, Iran and Western peacekeepers. Beirut was split by the Green Line; an estimated 120,000–150,000 people died. The Taif Agreement (1989) set the terms of peace, and the fighting ended in October 1990.
summary.zh: 基督教民兵、巴勒斯坦游击队与穆斯林及左翼政党之间的紧张关系于1975年爆发，叙利亚、以色列、伊朗和西方维和部队相继卷入。贝鲁特被“绿线”一分为二；估计有12万至15万人丧生。1989年的《塔伊夫协议》奠定了和平框架，战事于1990年10月结束。

sources.title: F. Traboulsi, A History of Modern Lebanon (2nd ed., 2012)

name.zh: 第一次巴勒斯坦大起义

summary.en: A traffic accident in Gaza in December 1987 set off a mass uprising of Palestinians in the occupied territories, with strikes, boycotts and stone-throwing youths. It made the PLO a negotiating partner and led to the Oslo Accords of 1993; Hamas was founded during it.
summary.zh: 1987年12月加沙的一起交通事故引发被占领土上巴勒斯坦人的大规模起义，包括罢工、抵制和青年投掷石块。起义使巴解组织成为谈判对象，并促成1993年《奥斯陆协议》；哈马斯也在此期间成立。

sources.title: R. Khalidi, The Hundred Years' War on Palestine (2020)

note: Plotted at Jabalia refugee camp, where the uprising began.

summary.en: Near the end of the Iran–Iraq War, Iraqi aircraft dropped mustard gas and nerve agents on the Kurdish town of Halabja, killing an estimated 3,200–5,000 civilians. It came during the 1988 Anfal campaign against Iraq’s Kurds, though some studies treat it as a separate atrocity.
summary.zh: 两伊战争末期，伊拉克飞机向库尔德城镇哈莱卜杰投下芥子气和神经毒剂，估计造成3200至5000名平民死亡。袭击发生在1988年针对伊拉克库尔德人的“安法尔行动”期间，但一些研究将其视为一桩独立的暴行。

sources.title: Human Rights Watch, Genocide in Iraq: The Anfal Campaign against the Kurds (1993)

name.zh: 第一次纳戈尔诺-卡拉巴赫战争

summary.en: The Armenian-majority region of Nagorno-Karabakh sought to leave Soviet Azerbaijan, leading to pogroms, expulsions and, after 1991, full-scale war. Armenian forces took the region and surrounding districts by the 1994 ceasefire; some 30,000 died and over a million were displaced.
summary.zh: 以亚美尼亚人为主的纳戈尔诺-卡拉巴赫地区要求脱离苏维埃阿塞拜疆，引发屠杀、驱逐，并在1991年后演变为全面战争。到1994年停火时，亚美尼亚武装控制了该地区及周边地区；约三万人死亡，一百多万人流离失所。

sources.title: T. de Waal, Black Garden: Armenia and Azerbaijan through Peace and War (2003)

note: Azerbaijan retook the territory in wars in 2020 and 2023, after which almost all Karabakh Armenians left.

summary.en: A magnitude-7.6 quake on the North Anatolian Fault struck the industrial heartland east of Istanbul before dawn, killing over 17,000 people. Poorly built apartment blocks collapsed, and the response prompted new building codes and a thaw with Greece, which sent rescue teams.
summary.zh: 凌晨，北安纳托利亚断层上发生7.6级地震，袭击伊斯坦布尔以东的工业中心，造成一万七千多人死亡。劣质公寓楼大批倒塌，此后土耳其制定了新的建筑规范；希腊派出救援队，两国关系也因此回暖。

sources.title: USGS: M 7.6 Izmit, Turkey Earthquake of 17 August 1999

summary.en: A magnitude-6.6 earthquake directly beneath Bam in south-eastern Iran killed about 26,000 people and destroyed much of the Arg-e Bam, the world’s largest mud-brick citadel. The citadel and its landscape were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2004.
summary.zh: 伊朗东南部巴姆城正下方发生6.6级地震，约2.6万人遇难，世界上最大的土坯城堡巴姆古城大部分被毁。2004年巴姆城堡及其文化景观被列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产名录。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Bam and its Cultural Landscape

summary.en: After Georgia launched an offensive on Tskhinvali, the capital of breakaway South Ossetia, on 7–8 August 2008, Russian forces invaded, routed the Georgian army and advanced towards Tbilisi. Russia then recognised South Ossetia and Abkhazia as independent states.
summary.zh: 2008年8月7日至8日格鲁吉亚向分离地区南奥塞梯首府茨欣瓦利发动攻势后，俄军入侵，击溃格鲁吉亚军队并向第比利斯方向推进。随后俄国承认南奥塞梯和阿布哈兹为独立国家。

sources.title: Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on the Conflict in Georgia (Tagliavini Report, 2009)

summary.en: A few thousand Islamic State fighters routed far larger Iraqi army forces and seized Mosul; after the group declared a "caliphate", Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi made his first public appearance as its caliph in the city's Great Mosque. Iraqi and Kurdish forces with coalition air support retook the city in 2017 after a nine-month battle.
summary.zh: 数千名“伊斯兰国”武装分子击溃人数远多于己的伊拉克军队，占领摩苏尔；该组织宣布建立“哈里发国”后，阿布·贝克尔·巴格达迪以“哈里发”身份在城中大清真寺首次公开露面。2017年伊拉克和库尔德部队在联军空中支援下经九个月战斗收复该城。

sources.title: F. A. Gerges, ISIS: A History (2016)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant

summary.en: The Houthi movement seized Sana'a in September 2014 and forced President Hadi to flee; a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015. Fighting, blockade and famine created one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises, and the country remains divided.
summary.zh: 2014年9月胡塞运动占领萨那，迫使哈迪总统出逃；2015年沙特领导的联军介入。战争、封锁和饥荒造成世界上最严重的人道危机之一，该国至今仍处于分裂状态。

note: Ongoing; endYear marks the atlas horizon, not an end of the war.

summary.en: The death in morality-police custody of Mahsa (Jina) Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish woman detained for her headscarf, set off nationwide protests led by women and students. Security forces killed hundreds of protesters and the state executed several; the movement persisted in defiance of hijab rules.
summary.zh: 22岁的库尔德女子玛莎（吉娜）·阿米尼因头巾问题被道德警察拘押后死亡，引发以女性和学生为主导的全国抗议。安全部队打死数百名抗议者，国家还处决了数人；此后人们继续以违抗头巾规定的方式坚持抗争。

sources.title: UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran, report A/HRC/55/67 (2024)

summary.en: On 7 October 2023 Hamas-led militants attacked southern Israel, killing about 1,200 people and taking some 250 hostages. Israel’s air and ground war in Gaza killed tens of thousands of Palestinians, according to Gaza health authorities, displaced most of the population and caused famine; a ceasefire took hold in October 2025.
summary.zh: 2023年10月7日，哈马斯领导的武装人员袭击以色列南部，约1200人遇难，约250人被劫为人质。以色列随后在加沙发动空中和地面战争，据加沙卫生部门统计，数万巴勒斯坦人死亡，绝大多数居民流离失所，并出现饥荒；2025年10月停火生效。

sources.title: UN OCHA: Hostilities in the Gaza Strip and Israel, situation reports

note: Casualty figures are contested and still being revised; Palestinian figures come from the Gaza Ministry of Health, which the UN has generally found reliable. Recent events; endYear marks the October 2025 ceasefire.

story.en:
Early on 7 October 2023, a Jewish holiday, thousands of fighters led by Hamas broke through the Gaza border fence under rocket cover and attacked army posts, kibbutzim and a music festival in southern Israel. About 1,200 people, most of them civilians, were killed, the deadliest day in Israel's history, and some 250 people were taken into Gaza as hostages.

Israel declared war, cut off supplies and began one of the most intense bombing campaigns of the century, followed by a ground invasion. By October 2025 the Gaza health ministry counted more than 67,000 Palestinians killed, a large share of them women and children; most of Gaza's 2.1 million people were displaced, many repeatedly, and UN-backed experts confirmed famine in Gaza Governorate, around Gaza City, in August 2025 (Israel disputed the finding). South Africa brought a genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice, which Israel rejects, and the International Criminal Court issued warrants for Israeli and Hamas leaders.

The war spread to Lebanon, Yemen and direct Israeli–Iranian exchanges. A ceasefire in November 2023 and another in early 2025 freed some hostages; a US-brokered agreement in October 2025 led to the return of the remaining living hostages and the release of Palestinian prisoners, though Gaza's future remained unsettled.
story.zh:
2023年10月7日清晨，正值犹太节日，数千名由哈马斯领导的武装人员在火箭弹掩护下突破加沙边境围栏，袭击以色列南部的军事据点、基布兹和一场音乐节。约1200人遇难，其中大多数是平民，这是以色列历史上死亡人数最多的一天；约250人被掳往加沙作为人质。

以色列宣战，切断物资供应，展开本世纪最猛烈的轰炸之一，随后发动地面进攻。到2025年10月，加沙卫生部统计已有超过6.7万名巴勒斯坦人死亡，其中很大一部分是妇女和儿童；加沙210万人口中的大多数流离失所，许多人多次被迫迁徙，联合国支持的专家于2025年8月确认加沙城所在的加沙省出现饥荒（以色列对此结论提出异议）。南非向国际法院起诉以色列犯有种族灭绝罪，以色列予以否认；国际刑事法院也对以色列和哈马斯领导人发出逮捕令。

战火蔓延到黎巴嫩、也门，以色列与伊朗也发生直接交火。2023年11月和2025年初的两次停火释放了部分人质；2025年10月在美国斡旋下达成的协议使剩余在世人质获释、巴勒斯坦囚犯被释放，但加沙的前途仍悬而未决。

name.zh: 图格里勒率塞尔柱人进入巴格达

summary.en: Invited by the Abbasid caliph al-Qa'im, the Seljuk leader Tughril entered Baghdad in December 1055 and arrested al-Malik al-Rahim, the last Buyid emir of Iraq. The Sunni Seljuk sultans replaced the Shi'i Buyids as the caliphs' military masters and protectors.
summary.zh: 应阿拔斯哈里发卡伊姆之请，塞尔柱首领图格里勒于1055年12月进入巴格达，逮捕伊拉克的末代白益埃米尔马利克·拉希姆。信奉逊尼派的塞尔柱苏丹从此取代什叶派的白益王朝，成为哈里发的军事主宰与保护者。

story.en:
Since 945 the Abbasid caliphs had been figureheads in their own capital, controlled by the Shi'i Buyid emirs. By the 1050s the Buyid house was divided and weak, and the real master of Baghdad was the Turkish commander al-Basasiri, who was suspected of leaning toward the rival Fatimid caliphate in Cairo. Further east, Tughril and his brother Chaghri had defeated the Ghaznavids at Dandanaqan in 1040 and built a Seljuk state across Iran.

Caliph al-Qa'im turned to the Sunni Turkmen. Tughril reached Baghdad in December 1055 and the Friday sermon was read in his name. After his troops clashed with the townspeople, he arrested the Buyid emir al-Malik al-Rahim, who died in captivity a few years later.

The new order was soon tested. In 1058, while Tughril was fighting a rebel brother, al-Basasiri seized Baghdad and had the Friday prayer said for the Fatimid caliph for about a year. Tughril returned at the end of 1059, restored al-Qa'im, and his forces killed al-Basasiri. From then on the caliph granted legitimacy while the sultan held the sword, an arrangement that shaped the Sunni Middle East for two centuries.
story.zh:
自945年起，阿拔斯哈里发在自己的都城里沦为傀儡，受什叶派的白益埃米尔控制。到1050年代，白益家族四分五裂、日渐衰弱，巴格达真正的主人是突厥将领巴萨西里，他被怀疑倾向开罗的对手法蒂玛王朝。在更东方，图格里勒与其兄弟查格里已于1040年在丹丹坎击败伽色尼王朝，在伊朗建立起塞尔柱国家。

哈里发卡伊姆转而求助于信奉逊尼派的突厥蛮人。1055年12月图格里勒抵达巴格达，聚礼日的呼图白开始以他的名义诵读。其部队与市民发生冲突后，他逮捕了白益埃米尔马利克·拉希姆；后者数年后死于囚禁之中。

新秩序很快受到考验。1058年，趁图格里勒征讨叛乱的兄弟之际，巴萨西里夺取巴格达，并以法蒂玛哈里发的名义主持聚礼约一年之久。1059年底图格里勒返回，恢复卡伊姆之位，其部队击杀了巴萨西里。此后，哈里发授予合法性，苏丹执掌兵权，这一格局塑造了此后两个世纪的逊尼派中东。

sources.title: A. C. S. Peacock, The Great Seljuk Empire (2015)

note: No Wikidata item exists for this event. Sources date Tughril's own entry to mid-December 1055 (447 AH); al-Basasiri's interlude ran from December 1058 to December 1059.

name.zh: 伽色尼的马哈茂德攻取剌夷

summary.en: Called in by the Buyid ruler of Rayy, Majd al-Dawla, against his own mutinous Daylamite troops, Mahmud of Ghazni instead deposed him, sacked the city and burned books judged heretical. Ghaznavid rule in western Iran was short-lived: the Seljuks took Khurasan in 1040 and Rayy soon after.
summary.zh: 剌夷的白益统治者马吉德·道莱为对付哗变的德莱木部队，请伽色尼的马哈茂德前来援助，后者却废黜了他，洗劫该城，并焚毁被视为异端的书籍。伽色尼王朝在伊朗西部的统治十分短暂：1040年塞尔柱人夺取呼罗珊，不久又攻占剌夷。

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth, The Ghaznavids: Their Empire in Afghanistan and Eastern Iran (1963)

note: QID is the wider Ghaznavid campaigns in Persia (1012–1034). Sources place the capture between March and May 1029, and differ on how much of Rayy's library was destroyed.

summary.en: Kuwait and Britain ended the protection agreement of 1899, and Emir Abdullah al-Salim Al Sabah proclaimed full independence. When Iraq's leader Abd al-Karim Qasim claimed Kuwait days later, British forces landed in July (Operation Vantage) and were relieved by an Arab League force; Iraq recognised Kuwait in 1963.
summary.zh: 科威特与英国终止1899年的保护协定，埃米尔阿卜杜拉·萨利姆·萨巴赫宣布完全独立。数日后伊拉克领导人阿卜杜勒-卡里姆·卡塞姆宣称科威特属于伊拉克，英军于7月登陆（“优势行动”），随后由阿拉伯联盟部队接防；伊拉克于1963年承认科威特。

sources.title: CIA Center for the Study of Intelligence: Gauging Iraq's threat to Kuwait in the 1960s

note: QID is Operation Vantage, the British deployment of July 1961; Wikidata has no separate item for the independence itself. Plotted at Kuwait City.

summary.en: In a British-backed palace coup at Salalah, Qaboos bin Said deposed his father, Sultan Said bin Taimur, whose isolationist rule had left the country with almost no schools or roads while the Dhofar rebellion spread. Qaboos renamed Muscat and Oman the Sultanate of Oman, spent oil revenue on modernisation and, with British and Iranian help, defeated the rebels by 1976.
summary.zh: 在英国支持下，卡布斯·本·赛义德在塞拉莱发动宫廷政变，废黜其父赛义德·本·泰穆尔苏丹；后者的闭关统治使国家几乎没有学校和道路，而佐法尔叛乱日益蔓延。卡布斯将“马斯喀特和阿曼”改名为阿曼苏丹国，用石油收入推动现代化，并在英国和伊朗协助下于1976年平定叛乱。

sources.title: University of Central Arkansas, Dynamic Analysis of Dispute Management: Oman (1912–present)
J. E. Peterson, Oman's Insurgencies: The Sultanate's Struggle for Supremacy (2007)
